tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice.

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background.

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: ReportFindings
tools.description: Report code-review findings as a typed list so the host UI can render them. Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

level.description: Effort level the review ran at

findings.description: Verified findings, most-severe first; empty if none survived

file.description: Repo-relative path of the file the finding is in

short_summary.description: Compressed label for compact UI (≤60 chars): the claim alone, no rationale or consequence clause

category.description: Short kebab-case slug of the finding type, e.g. "correctness", "simplification", "efficiency", "test-coverage"

verdict.description: Set when a verify pass ran; absent on inline-only reviews

outcome.description: Set ONLY when re-reporting after applying fixes: what happened to this finding

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: TaskStop
tools.description:
- Stops a running background task by its ID
- Takes a task_id parameter identifying the task to stop
- To stop an agent-team teammate, pass its agent ID or bare teammate name as task_id
- To stop a background agent spawned with a name, pass that name as task_id
- Returns a success or failure status
- Use this tool when you need to terminate a long-running task

task_id.description: The ID of the background task to stop. Agent-team teammates and named background agents are also accepted by agent ID or name.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: WebSearch
tools.description:
Search the web. Returns result blocks with titles and URLs. US-only.

- The current month is (provided in the conversation below) — use this when searching for recent information.
- `allowed_domains` / `blocked_domains` filter results.
- After answering from results, end with a "Sources:" list of the URLs you used as markdown links.

allowed_domains.description: Only include search results from these domains

blocked_domains.description: Never include search results from these domains

mode.description: "standard": the normal web search: quick and cheap; right for straightforward lookups (reference facts, official pages, documentation, well-known people, places and topics) and simple follow-up lookups. "extended": a thorough, fresh search at several times the cost and latency.

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

tools.name: DeferredToolPlaceholder
tools.description: Reserved placeholder that keeps deferred tool loading active; never call this tool.

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to write (must be absolute, not relative)

content.description: The content to write to the file

content.text: Tool loaded.

"""Copy this project's Claude Code session logs into ai-sessions/, redacting secrets.

    python scripts/export_sessions.py [--src <~/.claude/projects/<folder>>]

Copies the session .jsonl files, their tool-result files, and memory/ (Claude Code's auto-memory
for this project: the only standing instruction the agent had, which the brief asks for).
Redacted: anything shaped like an OpenAI key (sk-...), the employer's name and email domain,
and the Claude account email. Everything else is copied unedited. Re-run before submitting so the
folder holds the full, final sessions. Exits non-zero if anything key-shaped survives.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import re
import shutil
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
DEFAULT_SRC = Path.home() / ".claude" / "projects" / "c--Users-YashwanthYanala-Desktop-project"

# (?<![A-Za-z0-9]) so words like "task-notification" or "disk-cleanup" are left alone
RULES = [
    (re.compile(r"(?<![A-Za-z0-9])sk-[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{8,}"), "sk-REDACTED"),
    (re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9._%+\-]*@?[A-Za-z0-9.\-]*first[\s_\-]?distributors(?:\.com)?", re.I), "[employer redacted]"),
    (re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9._%+\-]*[account email redacted][A-Za-z0-9._%+\-]*(?:@[A-Za-z0-9.\-]+)?", re.I), "[account email redacted]"),
]
KEYLIKE = re.compile(r"(?<![A-Za-z0-9])sk-(?!REDACTED)[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{8,}")
LEFTOVER = re.compile(r"first[\s_\-]?distributors|[account email redacted]", re.I)


def redact(text: str) -> tuple[str, int]:
    n = 0
    for pat, rep in RULES:
        text, k = pat.subn(rep, text)
        n += k
    return text, n


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--src", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_SRC)
    ap.add_argument("--out", type=Path, default=ROOT / "ai-sessions")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    # check everything before deleting anything: a wrong --src must not wipe the last good export,
    # and --out must be this repo's ai-sessions folder, never a parent or a typo
    logs = list(a.src.glob("*.jsonl")) if a.src.is_dir() else []
    if not logs:
        sys.exit(f"no session logs (*.jsonl) in {a.src}; nothing deleted")
    if a.out.resolve().name != "ai-sessions" or a.out.resolve().parent != ROOT:
        sys.exit(f"--out must be {ROOT / 'ai-sessions'}; nothing deleted")
    if a.out.exists():
        shutil.rmtree(a.out)
    total, files = 0, 0
    for f in sorted(a.src.rglob("*")):
        if not f.is_file():
            continue
        dest = a.out / f.relative_to(a.src)
        dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        text = f.read_bytes().decode("utf-8", errors="surrogateescape")
        text, n = redact(text)
        dest.write_bytes(text.encode("utf-8", errors="surrogateescape"))
        total, files = total + n, files + 1
    left = [p for p in a.out.rglob("*") if p.is_file()
            and (KEYLIKE.search(t := p.read_text("utf-8", errors="replace")) or LEFTOVER.search(t))]
    print(f"{files} files -> {a.out} | {total} redactions | files with anything left to redact: {len(left)}")
    return 1 if left else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

content.text:
The code review is done. I fixed what it found, and the fixes are committed as `1d06114`.

**The review** read the parser (`rfq/`) and the helper scripts (`scripts/`). It found 10 problems, all in the helper scripts. It found nothing in the parser that produces `parsed.json`. I checked every finding against the code before changing anything, and all 10 were real.

**The ones that mattered for your submission:**

1. **The redaction was changing ordinary words.** My key filter looked for `sk-` anywhere, so "ta**sk-**notification" became "task-REDACTED" 22 times in the session logs. The brief says the logs must be unedited except for secrets. Now only real key-shaped text is redacted.
2. **The export script could delete the session logs.** It deleted the old `ai-sessions/` before checking that the source folder existed. Run on another machine, it would have wiped them and reported success. It now checks first and refuses if anything looks wrong.
3. **The cache cleanup script could delete the replay cache.** Given the wrong report, it would have deleted all 24 saved dev answers. Then the no-key run, which the graders do, would have fallen back to "needs review" for every email. It now refuses when the report doesn't match the cache.
4. **The quote desk and the scorer disagreed on quantity.** The desk ignored the allowed tolerance and didn't show missed lines. It now uses the scorer's own quantity check and lists any missed lines.

**A problem I caused while fixing:** my first rewrite of the redaction hung on the large images stored in the logs. I stopped it and rewrote it, and it now finishes in under a second.

**Checks after the fixes:**
- Dev score unchanged: 24/24 classes, 210/210 lines.
- Stress score unchanged: 118/133 lines.
- All 18 tests pass.
- The safety checks refuse bad input as intended.
- The session logs have 0 secrets, your employer's name or your account email left.

`ai-sessions/` now also includes the reviewer's own log, since the brief asks for every agent session.

**What's left:**
1. **The screen recording**, which you do. I'll write you a simple step-by-step script.
2. **Submit**: a final session export, then push to GitHub or zip.

Shall I write the recording script now?

content.text:
The two optional parts are in different states:

**1. The small web app: yes, built.**
It's [rfq/viewer.py](rfq/viewer.py), committed as `622a8be`, the local viewer you opened earlier. It covers what the brief asks for:
- the email and its attachments, as the model saw them;
- the extracted lines, where each came from, and clicking a line highlights it in the source;
- the answer-key check, the guard notes and the cost.

The part it lacks is "each line's catalog match, which a rep can accept or overturn", because that depends on the matcher. The hosted quote desk is extra and isn't part of the submission.

**2. The matcher: no.** It's mentioned in one line under "Known broken / next" in DECISIONS.md. Nothing is designed or built.

Here's what that part involves:
- `data/catalog.csv` has 937 stocked parts, each with structured columns: size, schedule/class, material, ends.
- The answer key has a match answer for every dev line: **194 lines "matched"** to one part and **16 "not in catalog"**.
- The trap the brief describes is a wrong part that's only one attribute off, for example the right size with the wrong schedule. That counts as a confident wrong match, and it's the worst failure.

**My recommendation:** the brief says the matcher is never penalised if skipped, and it's weighed only in the interview. You've spent about 5 of the 8–12 hours, so there's time.

- **At minimum, write `MATCHER.md` (design only, about 30 minutes).** It's one page covering what we normalise, which attributes must agree exactly, when the answer is "not in catalog" versus "ask the customer", and what the model may suggest but never decide. This is cheap, and interviewers will likely ask about it.
- **Optionally, build it as well (about 2–3 hours).** This would be a rule-based matcher in code that compares attributes, plus the `sku`/`match` fields, plus accept/overturn buttons in the viewer. We'd score it against the 210 dev answers. It's real extra work, and a rushed version with confident wrong matches would look worse than a clear design page.

Should I write the design page only, or design and build it? Either way the recording comes after, so it can show whichever you choose.

input.content:
"""Catalog matcher: an extracted line -> one stocked part, "not in catalog", or "ambiguous".

Code decides, not the model. A wrong part is a wrong quote, and every rule here can be
checked by a rep in one line of `match_reason`:

  1. Read the line's description into the catalog's own attributes: product, size, spec
     (schedule / pressure class), material, ends, and stated features (full port, inner ring...).
  2. Candidates = catalog parts with the same product and the same size. None -> not in catalog.
  3. Every attribute the customer STATED must agree. Nothing left -> not in catalog, and the
     reason names the nearest stocked part and what differs ("stocked only in SCH 80").
  4. Exactly one left -> matched. Several left -> they differ in something the customer didn't
     say -> ambiguous (ask the customer), never a guess.

The vocabulary is the catalog's, plus standard trade synonyms (README: Sch/Schedule, 150#/Class
150, BW/butt weld, threaded/NPT, SMLS/seamless, galv/galvanized). No dev-set strings.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import re
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path

# ---- products: (pattern, catalog product names). Specific before generic; first hit by
# position in the text wins, and "pipe" only counts when nothing else is named.
PRODUCTS: list[tuple[str, set[str]]] = [
    (r"swing\s*check|swing\s*chk", {"swing check valve"}),
    (r"check\s*valve|\bvlv\s*check|\bcheck\b", {"check valve", "swing check valve"}),
    (r"ball\s*valve|\bvlv\s*ball", {"ball valve"}),
    (r"gate\s*valve|\bvlv\s*gate", {"gate valve"}),
    (r"globe\s*valve|\bvlv\s*globe", {"globe valve"}),
    (r"butterfly|\bbfly\b", {"butterfly valve"}),
    (r"\by[\s-]*strainer|\bstrainer\b", {"y-strainer"}),
    (r"street\s*(?:elbow|ell)|\bst\s*ell\b", {"street elbow"}),
    (r"\b45\s*(?:°|deg(?:ree)?s?\.?)?\s*(?:lr\s*|sr\s*|long\s*radius\s*)?(?:elbow|ell)\b|(?:elbow|ell)s?,?\s*45\b", {"45 elbow"}),
    (r"\b90\s*(?:°|deg(?:ree)?s?\.?)?\s*(?:lr\s*|sr\s*|long\s*radius\s*|short\s*radius\s*)?(?:elbow|ell)\b|(?:elbow|ell)s?,?\s*90\b", {"90 elbow"}),
    (r"\b(?:elbow|ell)s?\b", {"90 elbow", "45 elbow"}),
    (r"concentric|\bconc\b", {"concentric reducer"}),
    (r"eccentric|\becc\b", {"eccentric reducer"}),
    (r"\breducer\b|\bred\b", {"concentric reducer", "eccentric reducer"}),
    (r"\bblind\b", {"blind flange"}),
    (r"slip[\s-]*on|\bs/?o\b\s*(?:flange|flg)|(?:flange|flg)\s*s/?o\b", {"slip-on flange"}),
    (r"weld[\s-]*neck|\bw/?n\b\s*(?:flange|flg)?|(?:flange|flg)\s*w/?n\b", {"weld neck flange"}),
    (r"\bflanges?\b|\bflg\b", {"blind flange", "slip-on flange", "weld neck flange"}),
    (r"spiral[\s-]*wound|\bspw\b", {"spiral wound gasket"}),
    (r"stud\s*bolt|\bstuds?\b", {"stud bolt"}),
    (r"heavy\s*hex\s*nut|\bhh\s*nut", {"heavy hex nut"}),
    (r"hex\s*cap\s*screw|\bhcs\b", {"hex cap screw"}),
    (r"spring\s*nut", {"channel spring nut"}),
    (r"hex\s*nut", {"hex nut"}),
    (r"half[\s-]*coupling|half[\s-]*cplg", {"half coupling"}),
    (r"coupling|\bcplg\b", {"coupling"}),
    (r"bushing|\bbush\b", {"hex bushing"}),
    (r"\bunion\b", {"union"}),
    (r"\bnipples?\b", {"nipple"}),
    (r"\bplugs?\b", {"plug"}),
    (r"\bcaps?\b", {"cap"}),
    (r"\btees?\b", {"tee"}),
    (r"clevis", {"clevis hanger"}),
    (r"pipe\s*clamp", {"pipe clamp"}),
    (r"threaded\s*rod|all[\s-]*thread", {"threaded rod"}),
    (r"strut|unistrut", {"strut channel"}),
    (r"thread\s*tape|ptfe\s*tape|teflon\s*tape", {"ptfe thread tape"}),
    (r"thread\s*dope|pipe\s*dope", {"pipe thread dope"}),
]
PIPE = (r"\bpipe\b", {"pipe"})
PIPE_LIKE = {"pipe", "nipple"}

# ---- materials: (pattern, predicate on the catalog material). Stainless grades are read
# first; carbon-steel words only apply when no stainless grade is named.
STAINLESS = [
    (r"316", lambda m: "316" in m),
    (r"304", lambda m: "304" in m),
    (r"stainless|\bss\b", lambda m: "SS" in m or "304" in m or "316" in m),
]
OTHER_MATERIALS = [
    (r"\ba105\b|forged\s*steel", lambda m: m == "A105"),
    (r"\bwpb\b|a234", lambda m: m == "A234 WPB"),
    (r"a106|seamless|\bsmls\b", lambda m: m == "A106B SMLS"),
    (r"\ba53\b|a53b|\berw\b", lambda m: m.startswith("A53")),
    (r"galv", lambda m: "GALV" in m),
    (r"\bblack\b", lambda m: "BLACK" in m),
    (r"malleable|\bmi\b", lambda m: m.startswith("MI ")),
    (r"bronze", lambda m: m == "BRONZE"),
    (r"brass", lambda m: m == "BRASS"),
    (r"cast\s*iron|\bci\b", lambda m: m == "CAST IRON"),
    (r"\bwcb\b|a216", lambda m: m == "WCB"),
    (r"\bb8m\b", lambda m: m.startswith("B8M")),
    (r"\bb7\b", lambda m: m.startswith("B7")),

    (r"butt[\s-]*weld|\bbw\b", {"BW"}),
    (r"socket[\s-]*weld|\bsw\b", {"SW"}),
    (r"raised\s*face|\brf\b", {"RF"}),
    (r"flat\s*face|\bff\b", {"FF"}),
    (r"ring[\s-]*(?:type[\s-]*)?joint|\brtj\b", {"RTJ"}),
    (r"thread|\bthd\b|\b[fm]?npt\b|\bmpt\b|\bfpt\b|screwed", {"THD"}),

    (r"full\s*port|\bfp\b", "full port"),
    (r"(?:std|standard|reduced|regular)\s*port", "std port"),

    sku: str
    description: str
    product: str
    size: str
    spec: str
    material: str
    ends: str
    extra: str


@dataclass
class Wanted:
    products: set[str] = field(default_factory=set)
    size: str | None = None
    specs: set[str] = field(default_factory=set)
    material: list = field(default_factory=list)  # predicates, all must hold
    material_words: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    ends: set[str] | None = None
    ends_word: str = ""
    features: set[str] = field(default_factory=set)


def load_catalog(path: Path) -> list[Part]:
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
        return [Part(**{k: (r[k] or "").strip() for k in Part.__dataclass_fields__}) for r in csv.DictReader(f)]


def _norm_text(s: str) -> str:
    s = s.replace("″", '"').replace("”", '"').replace("“", '"').replace("°", "°")
    s = re.sub(r"(\d+)\s+(\d+/\d+)", r"\1-\2", s)  # 1 1/2 -> 1-1/2
    s = re.sub(r"(\d+)(\.\d+)", lambda m: f"{m[1]}-{FRACTIONS[m[2]]}" if m[2] in FRACTIONS else m[0], s)
    s = re.sub(r"\b0-(\d+/\d+)", r"\1", s)  # 0.75 -> 0-3/4 -> 3/4
    return s


def _size(s: str) -> str | None:
    for m in SIZE.finditer(s):
        a, mark_a, b, mark_b = m.groups()
        if not (mark_a or mark_b):
            continue  # a bare number is a qty, a class or a length, not a size
        return f"{a} x {b.lower()}" if b else a
    return None


def read_line(description: str) -> Wanted:
    s = _norm_text(description)
    low = s.lower()
    w = Wanted()

    hits = []
    for pat, names in PRODUCTS:
        m = re.search(pat, low)
        if m:
            hits.append((m.start(), names))
    if hits:
        w.products = min(hits, key=lambda h: h[0])[1]
    elif re.search(PIPE[0], low):
        w.products = PIPE[1]

    w.size = _size(s)

    for m in re.finditer(r"\bsch(?:edule)?\.?\s*(\d+)\s*(s)?\b", low):
        w.specs.add(f"SCH {m[1]}{'S' if m[2] else ''}")

        w.specs.add(f"{m[1] or m[2] or m[3]}#")
    for m in re.finditer(r"\b(\d{3,4})\s*(?:psi\s*)?wog\b", low):
        w.specs.add(f"{m[1]} WOG")
    if re.search(r"\bstd\b(?!\s*port)|\bstandard\s*wall", low) and not w.specs:
        w.specs.add("SCH 40")
    if re.search(r"\bxs\b|extra\s*strong", low) and not w.specs:
        w.specs.add("SCH 80")

    stainless = [(p, f) for p, f in STAINLESS if re.search(p, low)]
    for pat, pred in stainless or []:
        w.material.append(pred)
        w.material_words.append(re.search(pat, low)[0])
        break  # the most specific grade named
    for pat, pred in OTHER_MATERIALS:
        if stainless and pat.startswith(("\\ba105", "\\bwpb", "a106", "\\ba53", "carbon")):
            continue
        m = re.search(pat, low)
        if m:
            w.material.append(pred)
            w.material_words.append(m[0])

    is_pipe = bool(w.products & PIPE_LIKE)
    for pat, codes in PIPE_ENDS if is_pipe else ENDS:
        m = re.search(pat, low)
        if m:
            w.ends, w.ends_word = codes, m[0]
            break

    for pat, name in FEATURES:
        if re.search(pat, low):
            w.features.add(name)
    return w


@dataclass
class Match:
    match: str  # matched | not_in_catalog | ambiguous
    sku: str | None
    reason: str
    candidates: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)

    def fields(self) -> dict:
        d = {"sku": self.sku, "match": self.match, "match_reason": self.reason}
        if self.match == "ambiguous" and self.candidates:
            d["candidates"] = self.candidates
        return d


def _misses(p: Part, w: Wanted) -> list[str]:
    """Stated attributes this part does not satisfy, in words a rep reads."""
    out = []
    if w.specs and p.spec not in w.specs:
        out.append(f"{p.spec or 'no rating'} not {'/'.join(sorted(w.specs))}")
    if w.material and not all(f(p.material) for f in w.material):
        out.append(f"{p.material or 'no material'} not {' '.join(w.material_words)}")
    if w.ends and p.ends not in w.ends:
        out.append(f"{p.ends or 'no end type'} not {w.ends_word}")
    extra = p.extra.lower()
    for feat in sorted(w.features):
        if feat.lower() not in extra and not (feat == "std port" and "std port" in extra):
            out.append(f"no {feat}")
    return out


def match_line(description: str, catalog: list[Part]) -> Match:
    w = read_line(description)
    if not w.products or not w.size:
        what = "product" if not w.products else "size"
        return Match("ambiguous", None, f"could not read the {what} from the description; a rep must pick the part")

    same = [p for p in catalog if p.product in w.products and p.size == w.size]
    if not same:
        kinds = " or ".join(sorted(w.products))
        return Match("not_in_catalog", None, f'no {kinds} stocked in {w.size}"')

    fits = [p for p in same if not _misses(p, w)]
    if not fits:
        near = min(same, key=lambda p: (len(_misses(p, w)), p.sku))
        return Match("not_in_catalog", None,
                     f"nearest stocked part {near.sku} {near.description} is off: {'; '.join(_misses(near, w))}")
    if len(fits) == 1:
        p = fits[0]
        return Match("matched", p.sku, f"{p.description}: the only stocked part with every stated attribute")

    differ = [a for a in ("product", "spec", "material", "ends", "extra") if len({getattr(p, a) for p in fits}) > 1]
    return Match("ambiguous", None,
                 f"{len(fits)} stocked parts fit; customer did not state {', '.join(differ)}",
                 [p.sku for p in fits])


def match_all(parsed: dict, catalog: list[Part]) -> None:
    """Add sku / match / match_reason (and candidates) to every line, in place."""
    for rec in parsed.values():
        for ln in rec.get("line_items") or []:
            try:
                ln.update(match_line(ln.get("description") or "", catalog).fields())
            except Exception as e:  # a matcher bug must never cost the parse
                ln.update({"sku": None, "match": "ambiguous", "match_reason": f"matcher error: {type(e).__name__}"})

    sku: str
    description: str
    product: str
    size: str
    spec: str
    material: str
    ends: str
    extra: str


@dataclass
class Wanted:
    products: set[str] = field(default_factory=set)
    size: str | None = None
    specs: set[str] = field(default_factory=set)
    material: list = field(default_factory=list)  # predicates, all must hold
    material_words: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    ends: set[str] | None = None
    ends_word: str = ""
    features: set[str] = field(default_factory=set)


def load_catalog(path: Path) -> list[Part]:
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
        return [Part(**{k: (r[k] or "").strip() for k in Part.__dataclass_fields__}) for r in csv.DictReader(f)]


def _norm_text(s: str) -> str:
    s = s.replace("\u2033", '"').replace("\u201d", '"').replace("\u201c", '"').replace("\u00b0", "°")
    s = re.sub(r"(\d+)\s+(\d+/\d+)", r"\1-\2", s)  # 1 1/2 -> 1-1/2
    s = re.sub(r"(\d+)(\.\d+)", lambda m: f"{m[1]}-{FRACTIONS[m[2]]}" if m[2] in FRACTIONS else m[0], s)
    s = re.sub(r"\b0-(\d+/\d+)", r"\1", s)  # 0.75 -> 0-3/4 -> 3/4
    return s


def _size(s: str) -> str | None:
    for m in SIZE.finditer(s):
        a, mark_a, b, mark_b = m.groups()
        if not (mark_a or mark_b):
            continue  # a bare number is a qty, a class or a length, not a size
        return f"{a} x {b.lower()}" if b else a
    return None


def read_line(description: str) -> Wanted:
    s = _norm_text(description)
    low = s.lower()
    w = Wanted()

    hits = []
    for pat, names in PRODUCTS:
        m = re.search(pat, low)
        if m:
            hits.append((m.start(), names))
    if hits:
        w.products = min(hits, key=lambda h: h[0])[1]
    elif re.search(PIPE[0], low):
        w.products = PIPE[1]

    w.size = _size(s)

    for m in re.finditer(r"\bsch(?:edule)?\.?\s*(\d+)\s*(s)?\b", low):
        w.specs.add(f"SCH {m[1]}{'S' if m[2] else ''}")
    for m in re.finditer(r"\b(\d{2,4})\s*(?:#|lbs?\b|-?pound)|\bclass\s*(\d{2,4})\b|\b(\d{2,4})\s*class\b", low):
        w.specs.add(f"{m[1] or m[2] or m[3]}#")
    for m in re.finditer(r"\b(\d{3,4})\s*(?:psi\s*)?wog\b", low):
        w.specs.add(f"{m[1]} WOG")
    if re.search(r"\bstd\b(?!\s*port)|\bstandard\s*wall", low) and not w.specs:
        w.specs.add("SCH 40")
    if re.search(r"\bxs\b|extra\s*strong", low) and not w.specs:
        w.specs.add("SCH 80")

    stainless = [(p, f) for p, f in STAINLESS if re.search(p, low)]
    for pat, pred in stainless or []:
        w.material.append(pred)
        w.material_words.append(re.search(pat, low)[0])
        break  # the most specific grade named
    for pat, pred in OTHER_MATERIALS:
        if stainless and pat.startswith(("\\ba105", "\\bwpb", "a106", "\\ba53", "carbon")):
            continue
        m = re.search(pat, low)
        if m:
            w.material.append(pred)
            w.material_words.append(m[0])

    is_pipe = bool(w.products & PIPE_LIKE)
    for pat, codes in PIPE_ENDS if is_pipe else ENDS:
        m = re.search(pat, low)
        if m:
            w.ends, w.ends_word = codes, m[0]
            break

    for pat, name in FEATURES:
        if re.search(pat, low):
            w.features.add(name)
    return w


@dataclass
class Match:
    match: str  # matched | not_in_catalog | ambiguous
    sku: str | None
    reason: str
    candidates: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)

    def fields(self) -> dict:
        d = {"sku": self.sku, "match": self.match, "match_reason": self.reason}
        if self.match == "ambiguous" and self.candidates:
            d["candidates"] = self.candidates
        return d


def _misses(p: Part, w: Wanted) -> list[str]:
    """Stated attributes this part does not satisfy, in words a rep reads."""
    out = []
    if w.specs and p.spec not in w.specs:
        out.append(f"{p.spec or 'no rating'} not {'/'.join(sorted(w.specs))}")
    if w.material and not all(f(p.material) for f in w.material):
        out.append(f"{p.material or 'no material'} not {' '.join(w.material_words)}")
    if w.ends and p.ends not in w.ends:
        out.append(f"{p.ends or 'no end type'} not {w.ends_word}")
    extra = p.extra.lower()
    for feat in sorted(w.features):
        if feat.lower() not in extra and not (feat == "std port" and "std port" in extra):
            out.append(f"no {feat}")
    return out


def match_line(description: str, catalog: list[Part]) -> Match:
    w = read_line(description)
    if not w.products or not w.size:
        what = "product" if not w.products else "size"
        return Match("ambiguous", None, f"could not read the {what} from the description; a rep must pick the part")

    same = [p for p in catalog if p.product in w.products and p.size == w.size]
    if not same:
        kinds = " or ".join(sorted(w.products))
        return Match("not_in_catalog", None, f'no {kinds} stocked in {w.size}"')

    fits = [p for p in same if not _misses(p, w)]
    if not fits:
        near = min(same, key=lambda p: (len(_misses(p, w)), p.sku))
        return Match("not_in_catalog", None,
                     f"nearest stocked part {near.sku} {near.description} is off: {'; '.join(_misses(near, w))}")
    if len(fits) == 1:
        p = fits[0]
        return Match("matched", p.sku, f"{p.description}: the only stocked part with every stated attribute")

    differ = [a for a in ("product", "spec", "material", "ends", "extra") if len({getattr(p, a) for p in fits}) > 1]
    return Match("ambiguous", None,
                 f"{len(fits)} stocked parts fit; customer did not state {', '.join(differ)}",
                 [p.sku for p in fits])


def match_all(parsed: dict, catalog: list[Part]) -> None:
    """Add sku / match / match_reason (and candidates) to every line, in place."""
    for rec in parsed.values():
        for ln in rec.get("line_items") or []:
            try:
                ln.update(match_line(ln.get("description") or "", catalog).fields())
            except Exception as e:  # a matcher bug must never cost the parse
                ln.update({"sku": None, "match": "ambiguous", "match_reason": f"matcher error: {type(e).__name__}"})

import json
import time
import traceback
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from pathlib import Path

from .guards import fallback, finalize, missing_rows
from .ingest import Email, load_email
from .llm import LLM, ModelUnavailable
from .prompt import INSTRUCTIONS, PROMPT_VERSION, REQUEST_CLASSES, build_input
from .threads import link


def process_one(path: Path, llm: LLM) -> tuple[Email, dict, dict]:
    stats = {"model_calls": 0, "cached": False, "usage": None, "cost_usd": 0.0, "seconds": 0.0, "warnings": [], "fallback": None}
    em = Email(id=path.stem)
    try:
        em = load_email(path)

        content, schema, truncated = build_input(em)
        req = llm.request(INSTRUCTIONS, content, schema)
        res = llm.call(req, label=f"{PROMPT_VERSION}:{em.id}")
        _account(stats, res)
        record, warns = finalize(em, res.data, truncated)
        stats["model_reason"] = res.data.get("classification_reason")

        # Code checks completeness; the model gets one pointed second look (also cached).
        missed = missing_rows(em, record["line_items"]) if record["classification"] in REQUEST_CLASSES else {}
        if missed:
            listing = "\n".join(f"- from {f}: {r}" for f, rows in missed.items() for r in rows)
            stats["coverage_retry"] = listing
            note = (
                "CHECK: your previous answer did not include these numbered rows:\n" + listing +
                "\nRe-read the email. Return the complete answer again: include each of these rows "
                "if the customer is asking for it; leave a row out only if it is not requested "
                "(heading, crossed out, superseded, not among the accepted items)."
            )
            req2 = llm.request(INSTRUCTIONS, content + [{"type": "input_text", "text": note}], schema)
            try:
                res2 = llm.call(req2, label=f"{PROMPT_VERSION}:{em.id}:coverage")
                _account(stats, res2)
                record2, warns2 = finalize(em, res2.data, truncated)
                left = missing_rows(em, record2["line_items"])
                if record2["classification"] == record["classification"] and sum(map(len, left.values())) < sum(map(len, missed.values())):
                    record, warns, missed = record2, warns2, left
            except ModelUnavailable as e:
                warns.append(f"coverage retry failed: {e}")
            if missed:
                warns.append(f"model left out numbered rows after a second look (judged not requested): {missed}")

        stats["fallback"] = str(e)
        record = fallback(em, str(e))
    except Exception as e:  # a bug of ours must not cost the customer their answer
        stats["fallback"] = f"internal error: {type(e).__name__}: {e}"
        stats["traceback"] = traceback.format_exc(limit=5)
        record = fallback(em, f"internal error: {type(e).__name__}")

        results = list(ex.map(lambda p: process_one(p, llm), paths))

    emails = {em.id: em for em, _, _ in results}
    out = {em.id: rec for em, rec, _ in results}

    )

def _report(stats: dict, llm: LLM, secs: float) -> dict:
    tot = {"emails": len(stats), "model_calls": 0, "cache_hits": 0, "fallbacks": 0,
           "input_tokens": 0, "cached_input_tokens": 0, "output_tokens": 0, "reasoning_tokens": 0,
           "cost_usd_this_run": 0.0, "cost_usd_if_uncached": 0.0}

        tot["model_calls"] += st["model_calls"]
        tot["cache_hits"] += int(st["cached"])
        tot["fallbacks"] += int(bool(st["fallback"]))

                tot[k] += st["usage"][k]
            from .llm import cost_usd
            tot["cost_usd_if_uncached"] += cost_usd(llm.model, st["usage"]) or 0.0
        tot["cost_usd_this_run"] += st["cost_usd"] or 0.0
    n = max(1, sum(1 for st in stats.values() if st["usage"]))
    tot["avg_cost_usd_per_email"] = round(tot["cost_usd_if_uncached"] / n, 5)
    tot["avg_tokens_per_email"] = round((tot["input_tokens"] + tot["output_tokens"]) / n)
    tot["cost_usd_this_run"] = round(tot["cost_usd_this_run"], 5)
    tot["cost_usd_if_uncached"] = round(tot["cost_usd_if_uncached"], 5)
    tot["wall_seconds"] = round(secs, 1)
    return {"model": llm.model, "effort": llm.effort, "prompt_version": PROMPT_VERSION, "totals": tot, "emails": stats}

from .guards import fallback, finalize, missing_rows
from .ingest import Email, load_email
from .llm import LLM, ModelUnavailable
from .prompt import INSTRUCTIONS, PROMPT_VERSION, REQUEST_CLASSES, build_input
from .threads import link


def process_one(path: Path, llm: LLM) -> tuple[Email, dict, dict]:
    stats = {"model_calls": 0, "cached": False, "usage": None, "cost_usd": 0.0, "seconds": 0.0, "warnings": [], "fallback": None}
    em = Email(id=path.stem)
    try:
        em = load_email(path)
        stats["warnings"] += em.errors
        content, schema, truncated = build_input(em)
        req = llm.request(INSTRUCTIONS, content, schema)
        res = llm.call(req, label=f"{PROMPT_VERSION}:{em.id}")
        _account(stats, res)
        record, warns = finalize(em, res.data, truncated)
        stats["model_reason"] = res.data.get("classification_reason")

        # Code checks completeness; the model gets one pointed second look (also cached).
        missed = missing_rows(em, record["line_items"]) if record["classification"] in REQUEST_CLASSES else {}
        if missed:
            listing = "\n".join(f"- from {f}: {r}" for f, rows in missed.items() for r in rows)
            stats["coverage_retry"] = listing
            note = (
                "CHECK: your previous answer did not include these numbered rows:\n" + listing +
                "\nRe-read the email. Return the complete answer again: include each of these rows "
                "if the customer is asking for it; leave a row out only if it is not requested "
                "(heading, crossed out, superseded, not among the accepted items)."
            )
            req2 = llm.request(INSTRUCTIONS, content + [{"type": "input_text", "text": note}], schema)
            try:
                res2 = llm.call(req2, label=f"{PROMPT_VERSION}:{em.id}:coverage")
                _account(stats, res2)
                record2, warns2 = finalize(em, res2.data, truncated)
                left = missing_rows(em, record2["line_items"])
                if record2["classification"] == record["classification"] and sum(map(len, left.values())) < sum(map(len, missed.values())):
                    record, warns, missed = record2, warns2, left
            except ModelUnavailable as e:
                warns.append(f"coverage retry failed: {e}")
            if missed:
                warns.append(f"model left out numbered rows after a second look (judged not requested): {missed}")
        stats["warnings"] += warns
    except ModelUnavailable as e:
        stats["fallback"] = str(e)
        record = fallback(em, str(e))
    except Exception as e:  # a bug of ours must not cost the customer their answer
        stats["fallback"] = f"internal error: {type(e).__name__}: {e}"
        stats["traceback"] = traceback.format_exc(limit=5)
        record = fallback(em, f"internal error: {type(e).__name__}")
    return em, record, stats


def _account(stats: dict, res) -> None:
    """Add one call's tokens and cost to the email's stats (a cache hit adds tokens, not cost)."""
    keys = stats.setdefault("cache_keys", [])
    keys.append(res.key)
    stats["cache_key"] = keys[0]
    stats["cached"] = res.cached if len(keys) == 1 else stats["cached"] and res.cached
    if stats["usage"] is None:
        stats["usage"] = dict(res.usage)
    else:
        for k, v in res.usage.items():
            stats["usage"][k] = stats["usage"].get(k, 0) + v
    stats["seconds"] = round(stats["seconds"] + res.seconds, 2)
    if not res.cached:
        stats["model_calls"] += 1
        stats["cost_usd"] = (stats["cost_usd"] or 0) + (res.cost_usd or 0)


def run(email_dir: Path, out_path: Path, llm: LLM, workers: int = 4, catalog: Path | None = None) -> dict:
    paths = sorted(email_dir.glob("*.eml"))
    t0 = time.monotonic()
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=max(1, workers)) as ex:
        results = list(ex.map(lambda p: process_one(p, llm), paths))

    emails = {em.id: em for em, _, _ in results}
    out = {em.id: rec for em, rec, _ in results}
    stats = {em.id: st for em, _, st in results}
    try:
        link(emails, out)
    except Exception as e:  # links are a nice-to-have; never lose the per-email answers over them
        for st in stats.values():
            st["warnings"].append(f"thread linking failed: {e}")

    # catalog matching is code only (no model calls), so it runs on every replay as well
    matching = None
    if catalog is not None and catalog.is_file():
        try:
            match_all(out, load_catalog(catalog))
            matching = dict(Counter(ln["match"] for rec in out.values() for ln in rec["line_items"]))
        except Exception as e:  # optional; never lose the parse over it
            matching = {"error": f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"}

    out_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    out_path.write_text(json.dumps(out, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    report = _report(stats, llm, time.monotonic() - t0)
    report["totals"]["catalog_matching"] = matching
    out_path.with_name(out_path.stem + ".report.json").write_text(
        json.dumps(report, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n", encoding="utf-8"
    )
    return report


def _report(stats: dict, llm: LLM, secs: float) -> dict:
    tot = {"emails": len(stats), "model_calls": 0, "cache_hits": 0, "fallbacks": 0,
           "input_tokens": 0, "cached_input_tokens": 0, "output_tokens": 0, "reasoning_tokens": 0,
           "cost_usd_this_run": 0.0, "cost_usd_if_uncached": 0.0}
    for st in stats.values():
        tot["model_calls"] += st["model_calls"]
        tot["cache_hits"] += int(st["cached"])
        tot["fallbacks"] += int(bool(st["fallback"]))
        if st["usage"]:
            for k in ("input_tokens", "cached_input_tokens", "output_tokens", "reasoning_tokens"):
                tot[k] += st["usage"][k]
            from .llm import cost_usd
            tot["cost_usd_if_uncached"] += cost_usd(llm.model, st["usage"]) or 0.0
        tot["cost_usd_this_run"] += st["cost_usd"] or 0.0
    n = max(1, sum(1 for st in stats.values() if st["usage"]))
    tot["avg_cost_usd_per_email"] = round(tot["cost_usd_if_uncached"] / n, 5)
    tot["avg_tokens_per_email"] = round((tot["input_tokens"] + tot["output_tokens"]) / n)
    tot["cost_usd_this_run"] = round(tot["cost_usd_this_run"], 5)
    tot["cost_usd_if_uncached"] = round(tot["cost_usd_if_uncached"], 5)
    tot["wall_seconds"] = round(secs, 1)
    return {"model": llm.model, "effort": llm.effort, "prompt_version": PROMPT_VERSION, "totals": tot, "emails": stats}

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from .config import ROOT, api_key
from .llm import LLM
from .pipeline import run

DEFAULT_MODEL = "gpt-5.4-mini-2026-03-17"
DEFAULT_EFFORT = "medium"  # bake-off on dev: low skimmed rules (ditto marks), gpt-5.5 cost 4.6x for no gain


def main(argv=None) -> int:
    sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")
    sys.stderr.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="rfq")
    sub = ap.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
    p = sub.add_parser("parse", help="parse every .eml in a directory")
    p.add_argument("--emails", type=Path, required=True)
    p.add_argument("--out", type=Path, required=True)
    p.add_argument("--model", default=os.environ.get("RFQ_MODEL", DEFAULT_MODEL))
    p.add_argument("--effort", default=os.environ.get("RFQ_EFFORT", DEFAULT_EFFORT), choices=["none", "minimal", "low", "medium", "high"])
    p.add_argument("--cache", type=Path, default=ROOT / "cache")
    p.add_argument("--workers", type=int, default=4)
    p.add_argument("--offline", action="store_true", help="never call the model; cache only")
    a = ap.parse_args(argv)

    if not a.emails.is_dir():
        print(f"--emails {a.emails} is not a directory", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    key = None if a.offline else api_key()
    if key is None:
        print("no OPENAI_API_KEY: replaying from cache; uncached emails will be flagged for review", file=sys.stderr)
    llm = LLM(a.model, a.effort, a.cache, key)
    rep = run(a.emails, a.out, llm, a.workers)
    t = rep["totals"]
    print(
        f"{t['emails']} emails -> {a.out} | model {rep['model']} ({rep['effort']}) | "
        f"new calls {t['model_calls']}, cache hits {t['cache_hits']}, fallbacks {t['fallbacks']} | "
        f"this run ${t['cost_usd_this_run']:.4f}, full inbox uncached ${t['cost_usd_if_uncached']:.4f} "
        f"(${t['avg_cost_usd_per_email']:.4f}/email, ~{t['avg_tokens_per_email']} tokens/email) | {t['wall_seconds']}s",
        file=sys.stderr,
    )
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

            u_ok = (ln["uom"] or "EA") == (kk["uom"] or "EA")
            c["uom_ok"] += u_ok

    print(f"silent losses        {c['silent']}")
    print(f"hallucinated lines   {c['halluc']}")
    print(f"lost / phantom       {c['lost']} / {c['phantom']}")
    print(f"classification       {c['cls_ok']}/{c['emails']} {pct(c['cls_ok'], c['emails'])}")
    print(f"line recall          {c['paired']}/{c['key_lines']} {pct(c['paired'], c['key_lines'])}")
    print(f"line precision       {c['paired']}/{c['our_lines']} {pct(c['paired'], c['our_lines'])}")
    print(f"qty | uom | source   {pct(c['qty_ok'], c['qty_n'])} | {pct(c['uom_ok'], c['paired'])} | {pct(c['src_ok'], c['paired'])}")
    print(f"context carried      {c['ctx_ok']}/{c['ctx_n']} {pct(c['ctx_ok'], c['ctx_n'])}")
    print(f"revises/duplicate_of {c['link_ok']}/{c['link_n']}")
    print(f"needs_review P / R   {pct(c['rv_tp'], c['rv_tp'] + c['rv_fp'])} / {pct(c['rv_tp'], c['rv_tp'] + c['rv_fn'])}")
    if problems:
        print(f"\n{len(problems)} problem(s)" + ("" if verbose else " (-v to list)"))
        if verbose:
            print("\n".join("  " + p for p in problems))
    return 0

"""Score parsed.json against an answer key the way data/README.md describes grading.

    python scripts/score.py parsed.json [data/dev/answer_key.json] [-v]

Our reading of the README, not the graders' code: lines are paired per email on `raw` tokens;
`must_mention` alternatives split on "|", compared case/space/punctuation-insensitively with the
README's listed spelling equivalences. Treat absolute numbers as approximate, deltas as real.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

REQ = {"rfq", "rfq_revision", "purchase_order"}

# README: "common spellings of the same spec count as equal"
EQUIV = [
    (r"\bschedule\b", "sch"),
    (r"\bclass\s*(\d+)", r"\1#"), (r"(\d+)\s*(lb|lbs|pound)\b", r"\1#"),
    (r"\bbutt\s*-?\s*weld(ed)?\b", "bw"),
    (r"\b(threaded|thrd|thd|npt)\b", "npt"),
    (r"\bseamless\b", "smls"),
    (r"\bgalvanized\b", "galv"),
    (r"\b(elbows?|ell)\b", "ell"), (r"\b(valves?|vlv)\b", "vlv"), (r"\b(flanges?|flg)\b", "flg"),
    (r"\b(gaskets?|gskt)\b", "gskt"), (r"\bspiral\s*-?\s*wound\b", "spw"),
    (r"\bmalleable(\s*iron)?\b", "mi"), (r"\bcarbon\s*steel\b", "cs"), (r"\bfull\s*port\b", "fp"),
    (r"\b(reducers?|red)\b", "red"), (r"\b(couplings?|cplg)\b", "cplg"),
]


def canon(s: str) -> str:
    s = s.lower().replace("″", '"').replace("”", '"')
    for pat, rep in EQUIV:
        s = re.sub(pat, rep, s)
    return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9#/]", "", s)


def mentions(desc: str, phrase: str) -> bool:
    d = canon(desc)
    return any(canon(alt) and canon(alt) in d for alt in phrase.split("|"))


def toks(s: str) -> set[str]:
    return set(re.findall(r"[a-z0-9]+(?:[/.\-][a-z0-9]+)*", s.lower().replace("″", '"')))


def sim(a: str, b: str) -> float:
    ta, tb = toks(a), toks(b)
    return len(ta & tb) / len(ta | tb) if ta | tb else 0.0


def qty_ok(ln: dict, kk: dict) -> bool:
    """README: qty_tol is a relative tolerance (0 = exact); both null counts as agreeing."""
    if ln["qty"] is None or kk["qty"] is None:
        return ln["qty"] is None and kk["qty"] is None
    return abs(ln["qty"] - kk["qty"]) <= (kk.get("qty_tol") or 0) * abs(kk["qty"])


def pair(ours: list[dict], keys: list[dict], thresh: float = 0.5):
    cand = sorted(((sim(o["raw"], k["raw"]), i, j) for i, o in enumerate(ours) for j, k in enumerate(keys)), reverse=True)
    used_o, used_k, pairs = set(), set(), []
    for s, i, j in cand:
        if s < thresh:
            break
        if i in used_o or j in used_k:
            continue
        used_o.add(i)
        used_k.add(j)
        pairs.append((i, j))
    return pairs, [i for i in range(len(ours)) if i not in used_o], [j for j in range(len(keys)) if j not in used_k]


def main(argv) -> int:
    sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")
    verbose = "-v" in argv
    argv = [a for a in argv if a != "-v"]
    parsed = json.loads(Path(argv[0]).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    key = json.loads(Path(argv[1] if len(argv) > 1 else "data/dev/answer_key.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["emails"]

    c = dict(emails=0, cls_ok=0, silent=0, lost=0, phantom=0, key_lines=0, our_lines=0, paired=0,
             halluc=0, qty_ok=0, qty_n=0, uom_ok=0, src_ok=0, ctx_ok=0, ctx_n=0,
             link_ok=0, link_n=0, rv_tp=0, rv_fp=0, rv_fn=0)
    problems: list[str] = []
    for eid, k in sorted(key.items()):
        o = parsed.get(eid)
        c["emails"] += 1
        if o is None:
            problems.append(f"{eid}: MISSING")
            continue
        kc, oc = k["classification"], o["classification"]
        c["cls_ok"] += kc == oc
        if kc != oc:
            problems.append(f"{eid}: class {oc} (key {kc})")
        if kc in REQ and oc not in REQ:
            c["lost"] += 1
        if kc not in REQ and oc in REQ:
            c["phantom"] += 1
        needs_action = bool(k.get("line_items")) or k.get("needs_review")
        if needs_action and not o["line_items"] and not o["needs_review"]:
            c["silent"] += 1
            problems.append(f"{eid}: SILENT LOSS")
        for f in ("revises", "duplicate_of"):
            if k.get(f) or o.get(f):
                c["link_n"] += 1
                c["link_ok"] += k.get(f) == o.get(f)
                if k.get(f) != o.get(f):
                    problems.append(f"{eid}: {f} {o.get(f)} (key {k.get(f)})")
        kr, orv = bool(k.get("needs_review")), bool(o["needs_review"])
        c["rv_tp"] += kr and orv
        c["rv_fp"] += orv and not kr
        c["rv_fn"] += kr and not orv
        if kr != orv:
            problems.append(f"{eid}: needs_review {orv} (key {kr}) {o.get('review_reason') or ''}")

        kl, ol = k.get("line_items") or [], o["line_items"]
        c["key_lines"] += len(kl)
        c["our_lines"] += len(ol)
        pairs, extra, missed = pair(ol, kl)
        c["paired"] += len(pairs)
        c["halluc"] += len(extra)
        for i in extra:
            problems.append(f"{eid}: EXTRA line {ol[i]['raw']!r}")
        for j in missed:
            problems.append(f"{eid}: MISSED line {kl[j]['raw']!r}")
        for i, j in pairs:
            ln, kk = ol[i], kl[j]
            if kk.get("qty_tol") is not None:
                c["qty_n"] += 1
                q_ok = qty_ok(ln, kk)
                c["qty_ok"] += q_ok
                if not q_ok:
                    problems.append(f"{eid}: qty {ln['qty']} (key {kk['qty']}) on {kk['raw']!r}")
            u_ok = (ln["uom"] or "EA") == (kk["uom"] or "EA")
            c["uom_ok"] += u_ok
            if not u_ok:
                problems.append(f"{eid}: uom {ln['uom']} (key {kk['uom']}) on {kk['raw']!r}")
            s_ok = ln["source"] == kk["source"]
            c["src_ok"] += s_ok
            if not s_ok:
                problems.append(f"{eid}: source {ln['source']} (key {kk['source']})")
            must, mustnt = kk.get("must_mention") or [], kk.get("must_not_mention") or []
            if must or mustnt:
                c["ctx_n"] += 1
                miss = [m for m in must if not mentions(ln["description"], m)]
                bad = [m for m in mustnt if mentions(ln["description"], m)]
                c["ctx_ok"] += not miss and not bad
                if miss or bad:
                    problems.append(f"{eid}: context {kk['raw']!r} -> {ln['description']!r} missing={miss} forbidden={bad}")
            # optional matcher (README): confident wrong = we named a part and the answer differs
            if "match" in ln and kk.get("match"):
                c["m_n"] += 1
                m_ok = ln["match"] == kk["match"] and ln.get("sku") == kk.get("sku")
                c["m_ok"] += m_ok
                c["m_wrong"] += ln["match"] == "matched" and not m_ok
                c["nic_n"] += kk["match"] == "not_in_catalog"
                c["nic_ok"] += kk["match"] == "not_in_catalog" and ln["match"] == "not_in_catalog"
                if not m_ok:
                    problems.append(f"{eid}: match {ln['match']}/{ln.get('sku')} (key {kk['match']}/{kk.get('sku')}) "
                                    f"on {ln['description']!r}: {ln.get('match_reason')}")

    pct = lambda a, b: f"{100 * a / b:.1f}%" if b else "n/a"  # noqa: E731
    print(f"silent losses        {c['silent']}")
    print(f"hallucinated lines   {c['halluc']}")
    print(f"lost / phantom       {c['lost']} / {c['phantom']}")
    print(f"classification       {c['cls_ok']}/{c['emails']} {pct(c['cls_ok'], c['emails'])}")
    print(f"line recall          {c['paired']}/{c['key_lines']} {pct(c['paired'], c['key_lines'])}")
    print(f"line precision       {c['paired']}/{c['our_lines']} {pct(c['paired'], c['our_lines'])}")
    print(f"qty | uom | source   {pct(c['qty_ok'], c['qty_n'])} | {pct(c['uom_ok'], c['paired'])} | {pct(c['src_ok'], c['paired'])}")
    print(f"context carried      {c['ctx_ok']}/{c['ctx_n']} {pct(c['ctx_ok'], c['ctx_n'])}")
    print(f"revises/duplicate_of {c['link_ok']}/{c['link_n']}")
    print(f"needs_review P / R   {pct(c['rv_tp'], c['rv_tp'] + c['rv_fp'])} / {pct(c['rv_tp'], c['rv_tp'] + c['rv_fn'])}")
    if c["m_n"]:
        print(f"matcher: confident wrong {c['m_wrong']} | not-in-catalog recall {c['nic_ok']}/{c['nic_n']} "
              f"{pct(c['nic_ok'], c['nic_n'])} | match accuracy {c['m_ok']}/{c['m_n']} {pct(c['m_ok'], c['m_n'])}")
    if problems:
        print(f"\n{len(problems)} problem(s)" + ("" if verbose else " (-v to list)"))
        if verbose:
            print("\n".join("  " + p for p in problems))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

class State:
    def __init__(self, emails: Path, parsed: Path, key: Path | None, catalog: Path | None = None):
        self.dir = emails
        self.parsed = json.loads(parsed.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        rp = parsed.with_name(parsed.stem + ".report.json")
        self.report = json.loads(rp.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) if rp.exists() else {"emails": {}}
        self.key = json.loads(key.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["emails"] if key else None
        self.catalog = load_catalog(catalog) if catalog and catalog.is_file() else []
        self.parts = {p.sku: p for p in self.catalog}
        self.decisions_path = parsed.with_name(parsed.stem + ".rep_decisions.json")
        self.decisions: dict = (json.loads(self.decisions_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
                                if self.decisions_path.exists() else {})
        self.token = secrets.token_urlsafe(24)
        self._emails: dict[str, Email] = {}
        self._lock = threading.Lock()

    def decide(self, eid: str, idx: int, action: str, sku: str, note: str) -> None:
        ln = self.parsed[eid]["line_items"][idx]
        if action == "accept":
            rec = {"action": "accept", "match": ln.get("match"), "sku": ln.get("sku")}
        elif action == "not_in_catalog":
            rec = {"action": "overturn", "match": "not_in_catalog", "sku": None}
        elif action == "sku" and sku in self.parts:
            rec = {"action": "overturn" if sku != ln.get("sku") else "accept", "match": "matched", "sku": sku}
        elif action == "clear":
            rec = None
        else:
            raise ValueError("unknown SKU" if action == "sku" else "unknown action")
        with self._lock:
            lines = self.decisions.setdefault(eid, {})
            if rec is None:
                lines.pop(str(idx), None)
            else:
                rec.update(system={"match": ln.get("match"), "sku": ln.get("sku")}, note=note[:300],
                           at=datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds"))
                lines[str(idx)] = rec
            tmp = self.decisions_path.with_suffix(".tmp")
            tmp.write_text(json.dumps(self.decisions, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
            os.replace(tmp, self.decisions_path)
