# DECISIONS

**Time spent:** about 8 hours.

## Who decides what

`ingest` (code) → **one model call per email** (`gpt-5.4-mini-2026-03-17`, effort medium, strict
JSON schema) → `guards` (code) → `threads` (code) → `matcher` (code; see [MATCHER.md](MATCHER.md)).

- **Code reads the files**, keeping the structure that carries meaning: hidden sheets and rows,
  merged headings and struck cells (xlsx/xls); tracked deletions (docx); PDF rows rebuilt from
  word positions, scans sent as images; zips unpacked; photos turned upright. A broken part
  becomes `unreadable` with a reason. It never raises.
- **The model judges.** It decides the class, which lines are requests, and the self-contained
  description (heading scope, overrides beat defaults, quoted history is not a request). The prompt
  states principles; its one example is invented, not a dev row.
- **Code checks every fact it can.**
  - Struck and hidden-only lines are dropped, whatever the model said.
  - Non-requests carry no lines.
  - A request with no lines, or an unreadable part, is always `needs_review`.
  - `source` must be a real part.
  - `raw` is snapped to its unique source row, because the model's copy varies run to run.
  - A numbered row that no line covers gets one more call naming it. That caught a dropped PO line
    in E015 ($0.004).

**Measured, not guessed.** I wrote a scorer implementing the README's grading, and a 22-email
**stress inbox** of situations dev lacks, with answers written **before** each run: tracked
changes, Spanish, an invoice with item lines, "make #3 twelve and kill #5", a byte-identical
redelivery, a 35-page PDF, a BOM in a zip, an iPhone HEIC photo.

| | classes | lines (recall/precision) | silent | hallucinated | context |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| dev | 24/24 | 210/210 · 210/210 | 0 | 0 | 172/173 |
| stress | 22/22 | 141/141 · 141/141 | 0 | 0 | 140/141 |

`scripts/verify.py` re-checks all of this, the keyless replay and the hygiene rules from a fresh
clone in about 15 s.

**Rejected:** gpt-5.5 (4.6× the cost, *worse* context: it "corrected" `A53B` to `A53 Grade B`);
two calls per email (double cost, same reading); `.doc`/`.msg` readers (untestable here, so
flagged instead).

## Something in the data that surprised you

The most request-shaped text in the inbox is usually not a request.
- E013's bounce carries a perfect numbered list of valves: it is *our own* RFQ to a supplier.
- E011 is a supplier's price list.
- E005's workbook is named `RevB` and hides a sheet `Rev A (old)`. A reader that loads every sheet
  quotes both revisions, and a model that sees the filename calls it a revision with no earlier
  email.

Meanwhile the real requests hide: in a merged cell two rows up (`ALL FITTINGS BW SCH 40 A234 WPB
UNLESS NOTED`, with one row overriding it to SCH 80), or on a photo of a nameplate. Most of the
accuracy came from *ingest* faithfully marking hidden, struck and merged structure, not from the
prompt.

A second surprise: **dev agrees with you too easily.** The matcher scored 210/210 on dev. A test
generated from the catalog, whose expected answers come from the catalog table and not from my
logic, then found **113 confident wrong matches**: grades matched too loosely, `A-105 class 150`
read as class 105.

## Something in the brief or README you disagree with

The README allows `needs_review` only on `rfq`, `rfq_revision` and `purchase_order`. But the
brief's costliest failure is "a customer who never hears back", and some non-requests need a
person: a bounce of *our quote to a customer*, a "we went with someone else" that should close a
quote, a buyer's out-of-office on a deadline job. Under the contract these come back `auto_reply`
/ `other` with nothing to act on.

**What I did:** kept the contract in `parsed.json` (guards enforce it, because it is scored). The
model also states a one-line reason for every classification, shown in `parsed.report.json` and
the viewer, so a person can see *why* something was set aside. In production I'd add a separate
`attention` field rather than overload `needs_review`. Not built.

## Predicted held-out numbers, and two kinds of email I expect to get wrong

Dev is 100% partly because I looked at it; stress is the fairer guide. For ~40 held-out emails:

| silent | hallucinated | lost/phantom | classes | recall / precision | qty · uom · source | context | review P / R | matcher wrong · NIC recall |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **0** | **2–5** | **1–2** | **~90%** | **~90% / ~95%** | **~95 · 97 · 97%** | **~85%** | **~80 / 90%** | **0–2 · ~85%** |

Silent is 0 because code flags any request that comes back with no lines; review recall beats
precision because I flag on doubt.

1. **Photos and scans of handwritten lists.** The model's reading is all there is. A misread
   `6`/`8`, a missed line or a `raw` that pairs badly costs qty and recall. Code can't check a
   picture, and the model flags too rarely.
2. **Terse revisions of an email that isn't in the inbox.** "Kill #5" needs the original list,
   so the "complete order as now intended" will be incomplete. The same boundary, Rev B / resend
   / "also add", is new rfq or revision? I chose "revision only if it changes an *earlier email*";
   held-out may draw it differently.

## How this runs for real

**Built:**
- a content-addressed cache (sha256 of model, effort, prompt and full content incl. image bytes;
  atomic writes);
- 3 retries with timeouts and a circuit breaker after 3 consecutive failures;
- a header-based fallback per email, and per-email isolation;
- windowed long PDFs;
- a per-email cost and token report.

**Not built:** the webhook, a queue, a database.

- **3,000 emails a day.** $0.0072 per email measured (about 3,940 tokens), so about **$22/day**.
  Median latency is 4.9 s and the worst 24 s; 3,000/day is ~2 a minute, so one worker keeps up.
  Design: the webhook stores the raw `.eml` and enqueues its hash; workers run `process_one`;
  thread linking becomes a lookup in a store of past emails by Message-ID, subject and domain.
- **Provider down for two hours.** After the retries, the breaker trips and the rest get the
  fallback: auto_reply/bulk by header, everything else `rfq` + `needs_review`. Fallbacks aren't
  cached, so the next run re-calls exactly those. For real: hold them in the queue with backoff
  and an alert. 250 emails on a person's desk is worse than a 2-hour delay.
- **A 300-page PDF.** Built. It's read in windows of 30 pages (16 if scanned), one cached call
  each: ~10 calls, ~$0.30. Each window also gets page 1 and the previous window's end as
  context-only, because a heading on page 2 can govern page 40. A failed window flags review
  and keeps what was read; past 300 pages the rest is flagged. Stress S18: 105/105 rows (the
  old 30-page cap lost 15). Not done: a relevance pass to skip spec-book pages that hold no
  items.
- **The same email delivered twice.** Built two ways. The redelivery hashes to the same cache
  key, so it's free, and `threads` marks the later one `duplicate_of` (stress S13 is a byte copy).
  For real, dedupe on Message-ID plus body hash at the webhook.

## Known broken / next

- `raw` read from pictures varies between runs (E023). The cache makes it stable, not right.
- Thread linking only sees the current inbox; there's no memory of last week.
- The matcher reads only our `description`, so a context miss upstream becomes a match miss.
- Next: the `attention` field, and the viewer's rep overturns as the matcher's live error rate.

The README's `needs_review` rule is kept exactly. Next to it, every email now has `attention`: a one-line action, or null:

| Email | `attention` |
|---|---|
| E013 bounce | "our email to sales@ironbridgevalve.example ('Quote request - 2in forged valves…') was not delivered: fix the address and resend" |
| E012, S07 | "customer is waiting for an answer about Q-26-04417: reply with status / ETA" |

| S05 | "invoice / payment message INV-88412: route to accounting" |
| E014, S16, S01 | none (marketing, out-of-office) |

All 10 match what I wrote down **before** building it. The official format checker accepts the field, the scores are unchanged, the viewer shows "➜ action", and there are 8 new tests. My invoice test caught a bug in my first version: "**Inv**oice" itself matched as an invoice number.

**The bigger find: three portability bugs**

The brief says graders may run on Windows, Linux, WSL or Docker with **Python 3.11+**. I had only ever run Python 3.12 on Windows, so I tested on 3.11 / Linux in Docker:
1. **Two lines used Python 3.12-only syntax.** On 3.11 the program **would not even start**: a total failure before they read a word. Both fixed, and every file now compiles on 3.11.

# What a reply carries of its history: quoted lines, "On ... wrote:", an Outlook header block,
# or the earlier message attached whole.
QUOTED = re.compile(
    r"(?:^>.*\n){2,}|^-{2,}\s*original message|^on\b.{3,200}\bwrote:\s*$|^_{8,}\s*\n\s*from:|^from:\s.+\n\s*(?:sent|date):",
    re.I | re.M)
# A change written against positions in a list it doesn't contain: "#3", "item 5", "rest stays".
BY_POSITION = re.compile(
    r"#\s*\d+\b|\b(?:item|line|row|no\.?)\s*#?\s*\d+\b|"
    r"\b(?:rest|everything else|all else|the others|remaining)\b.{0,25}\b(?:same|fine|ok|as is|unchanged|stays?)\b|"
    r"\bsame as (?:before|previous|last|my (?:last|previous|earlier))", re.I)


def unanchored_revisions(emails: dict[str, Email], out: dict[str, dict]) -> None:
    """A revision of a request we can't see, written as changes to positions we can't see, can't
    be turned into "the complete order as now intended". Flag it for a person instead of
    returning a partial order that looks complete. (Run after `revises` is linked.)"""
    for eid, rec in out.items():
        if rec.get("classification") != "rfq_revision" or rec.get("revises"):
            continue
        em = emails[eid]
        carries_history = bool(QUOTED.search(em.body or "")) or any(p.mime == "message/rfc822" for p in em.parts)
        if carries_history or not BY_POSITION.search(em.body or ""):
            continue
        rec["needs_review"] = True
        why = ("changes an earlier request by item position, but that request is not in this inbox and "
               "is not quoted: the complete order can't be rebuilt; find the original before quoting")
        rec["review_reason"] = "; ".join(x for x in (rec.get("review_reason"), why) if x)

content.text:
Weakness #2 is fixed and committed (`7fb810a`, plus the doc update `a98e418`). `verify --linux` passes 15/15.

**What changed.** A revision of an email we can't see, written as "make #2 eight, kill #4, rest stays the same", can't become "the complete order as now intended". Returning half an order that *looks* complete would be a wrong quote. Now:
- **Flagged by code** (whatever the model says) when all three hold: the original isn't in the inbox, nothing is quoted or attached, and the changes are by position.
- **Not flagged** when the original is quoted ("On … wrote:", `>` lines, or an Outlook header block) or attached, because the model can rebuild the order. Also not flagged when the customer sends a complete new list, or when the original *is* in the inbox (it's linked instead).

**Evidence**
- **S22** (positions only): flagged, no invented lines, with the reason "find the original before quoting".
- **S23** (original quoted): full order rebuilt, #3 → 12, #4 removed.
- 7 unit tests, including one where the model *didn't* flag and the code still does, plus the four cases that must stay unflagged.
- Fires on **nothing** in dev (byte-identical). Stress 144/144 lines, review 100%/100%. Cost $0.008.
- DECISIONS.md updated: what's left of this weakness is the judgement call (is "Rev B" a new request or a revision?), not the rebuilding.

**Next: #1, handwritten photos and scans.** The idea:
- Every email with a **picture** gets a **second, independent read** of just its pictures.
- Code compares the two reads line by line. Where they disagree on a line or a quantity ("6" vs "8"), the email is flagged with the exact line named.
- When both reads agree, nothing changes.

I'll add a messy handwriting-style stress photo, with its answers written first. It touches the 8 picture emails in dev and stress plus the new one, about $0.05.

Ready to go?
ok

Starting #1. The design, refined after thinking about the existing picture emails:
- **Trigger:** only emails where at least one extracted line came **from a picture** (a photo or a scanned page).
- **The second read** sees only the email text and its pictures, with a narrow task: "transcribe each requested line in the pictures: its text and its quantity as written". It has its own instructions and schema, and is cached like every call.
- **Code compares** the two reads, per picture:
  - a different **number of lines** → flag;
  - a paired line with a **different quantity** → flag, naming the line and both numbers;
  - a line the second read **couldn't find** at all → flag.
- **One trap to avoid:** for a nameplate photo, the quantity is in the email text ("quote 3 of these"), not in the picture. If the second read sees no quantity in the picture, that line's quantity isn't compared, to avoid false alarms.

Starting #1. The design, refined after thinking about the existing picture emails:
- **Trigger:** only emails where at least one extracted line came **from a picture** (a photo or a scanned page).
- **The second read** sees only the email text and its pictures, with a narrow task: "transcribe each requested line in the pictures: its text and its quantity as written". It has its own instructions and schema, and is cached like every call.
- **Code compares** the two reads, per picture:
  - a different **number of lines** → flag;
  - a paired line with a **different quantity** → flag, naming the line and both numbers;
  - a line the second read **couldn't find** at all → flag.
- **One trap to avoid:** for a nameplate photo, the quantity is in the email text ("quote 3 of these"), not in the picture. If the second read sees no quantity in the picture, that line's quantity isn't compared, to avoid false alarms.

First, how `LLM.request` passes the schema, so the second read can use its own:

"""Run the inbox: ingest -> model (cached) -> guards, per email in parallel; then thread links.

Every email is isolated: any exception for one email becomes a flagged record for that email
and the run carries on. The run always writes a complete parsed.json.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import time
import traceback
from collections import Counter
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from pathlib import Path

from .attention import add_attention
from .guards import fallback, finalize, missing_rows
from .ingest import Email, load_email
from .llm import LLM, ModelUnavailable
from .matcher import load_catalog, match_all
from .prompt import INSTRUCTIONS, PROMPT_VERSION, REQUEST_CLASSES, build_input, build_window_input, schema
from .threads import link


def process_one(path: Path, llm: LLM) -> tuple[Email, dict, dict]:
    stats = {"model_calls": 0, "cached": False, "usage": None, "cost_usd": 0.0, "seconds": 0.0, "warnings": [], "fallback": None}
    em = Email(id=path.stem)
    try:
        em = load_email(path)
        stats["warnings"] += em.errors
        content, schema, truncated = build_input(em)
        req = llm.request(INSTRUCTIONS, content, schema)
        res = llm.call(req, label=f"{PROMPT_VERSION}:{em.id}")
        _account(stats, res)
        record, warns = finalize(em, res.data, truncated)
        stats["model_reason"] = res.data.get("classification_reason")

        # Code checks completeness; the model gets one pointed second look (also cached).
        missed = missing_rows(em, record["line_items"]) if record["classification"] in REQUEST_CLASSES else {}
        if missed:
            listing = "\n".join(f"- from {f}: {r}" for f, rows in missed.items() for r in rows)
            stats["coverage_retry"] = listing
            note = (
                "CHECK: your previous answer did not include these numbered rows:\n" + listing +
                "\nRe-read the email. Return the complete answer again: include each of these rows "
                "if the customer is asking for it; leave a row out only if it is not requested "
                "(heading, crossed out, superseded, not among the accepted items)."
            )
            req2 = llm.request(INSTRUCTIONS, content + [{"type": "input_text", "text": note}], schema)
            try:
                res2 = llm.call(req2, label=f"{PROMPT_VERSION}:{em.id}:coverage")
                _account(stats, res2)
                record2, warns2 = finalize(em, res2.data, truncated)
                left = missing_rows(em, record2["line_items"])
                if record2["classification"] == record["classification"] and sum(map(len, left.values())) < sum(map(len, missed.values())):
                    record, warns, missed = record2, warns2, left
            except ModelUnavailable as e:
                warns.append(f"coverage retry failed: {e}")
            if missed:
                warns.append(f"model left out numbered rows after a second look (judged not requested): {missed}")
        if record["classification"] in REQUEST_CLASSES:
            _read_windows(em, record, llm, stats, warns, truncated)
        stats["warnings"] += warns
    except ModelUnavailable as e:
        stats["fallback"] = str(e)
        record = fallback(em, str(e))
    except Exception as e:  # a bug of ours must not cost the customer their answer
        stats["fallback"] = f"internal error: {type(e).__name__}: {e}"
        stats["traceback"] = traceback.format_exc(limit=5)
        record = fallback(em, f"internal error: {type(e).__name__}")
    return em, record, stats


def _read_windows(em: Email, record: dict, llm: LLM, stats: dict, warns: list[str], truncated: list[str]) -> None:
    """Long PDFs: one more cached call per window of pages; their lines are added to the record.
    A window that can't be read makes the email need review: lines would be missing."""
    seen = {(ln["source"], ln["raw"]) for ln in record["line_items"]}
    failed = []
    for part in em.parts:
        for k, w in enumerate(part.windows):
            content = build_window_input(em, part, k, record["classification"])
            req = llm.request(INSTRUCTIONS, content, schema(["body"] + [p.filename for p in em.parts]))
            try:
                res = llm.call(req, label=f"{PROMPT_VERSION}:{em.id}:{part.filename}:p{w['pages']}")
            except ModelUnavailable as e:
                failed.append(f"{part.filename} pages {w['pages']} could not be read ({e})")
                continue
            _account(stats, res)
            data = dict(res.data, classification=record["classification"])
            got, w_warns = finalize(em, data, truncated)
            warns += [f"{part.filename} p{w['pages']}: {x}" for x in w_warns]
            for ln in got["line_items"]:
                if ln["source"] != part.filename:
                    warns.append(f"{part.filename} p{w['pages']}: dropped a line credited to {ln['source']} "
                                 f"(a window may only add lines from its own pages): {ln['raw']!r}")
                elif (ln["source"], ln["raw"]) in seen:
                    warns.append(f"{part.filename} p{w['pages']}: dropped a repeat of an earlier line: {ln['raw']!r}")
                else:
                    seen.add((ln["source"], ln["raw"]))
                    record["line_items"].append(ln)
            stats.setdefault("windows", []).append(f"{part.filename} pages {w['pages']}: {len(got['line_items'])} line(s)")
    if failed:
        record["needs_review"] = True
        reasons = [r for r in (record.get("review_reason") or "").split("; ") if r]
        record["review_reason"] = "; ".join(dict.fromkeys(reasons + failed))


def _account(stats: dict, res) -> None:
    """Add one call's tokens and cost to the email's stats (a cache hit adds tokens, not cost)."""
    keys = stats.setdefault("cache_keys", [])
    keys.append(res.key)
    stats["cache_key"] = keys[0]
    stats["cached"] = res.cached if len(keys) == 1 else stats["cached"] and res.cached
    if stats["usage"] is None:
        stats["usage"] = dict(res.usage)
    else:
        for k, v in res.usage.items():
            stats["usage"][k] = stats["usage"].get(k, 0) + v
    stats["seconds"] = round(stats["seconds"] + res.seconds, 2)
    if not res.cached:
        stats["model_calls"] += 1
        stats["cost_usd"] = (stats["cost_usd"] or 0) + (res.cost_usd or 0)


def run(email_dir: Path, out_path: Path, llm: LLM, workers: int = 4, catalog: Path | None = None) -> dict:
    paths = sorted(email_dir.glob("*.eml"))
    t0 = time.monotonic()
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=max(1, workers)) as ex:
        results = list(ex.map(lambda p: process_one(p, llm), paths))

    emails = {em.id: em for em, _, _ in results}
    out = {em.id: rec for em, rec, _ in results}
    stats = {em.id: st for em, _, st in results}
    try:
        link(emails, out)
    except Exception as e:  # links are a nice-to-have; never lose the per-email answers over them
        for st in stats.values():
            st["warnings"].append(f"thread linking failed: {e}")

    # attention: non-requests that still need a person (code only; needs_review stays per README)
    add_attention(emails, out, stats)

    # catalog matching is code only (no model calls), so it runs on every replay as well
    matching = None
    if catalog is not None and catalog.is_file():
        try:
            match_all(out, load_catalog(catalog))
            matching = dict(Counter(ln["match"] for rec in out.values() for ln in rec["line_items"]))
        except Exception as e:  # optional; never lose the parse over it
            matching = {"error": f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"}

    out_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    # "\n" on every OS: the same inbox gives the same bytes on Windows, Linux, WSL and Docker
    out_path.write_text(json.dumps(out, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
    report = _report(stats, llm, time.monotonic() - t0)
    report["totals"]["catalog_matching"] = matching
    report["totals"]["attention"] = sum(1 for rec in out.values() if rec.get("attention"))
    out_path.with_name(out_path.stem + ".report.json").write_text(
        json.dumps(report, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n"
    )
    return report


def _report(stats: dict, llm: LLM, secs: float) -> dict:
    tot = {"emails": len(stats), "model_calls": 0, "cache_hits": 0, "fallbacks": 0,
           "input_tokens": 0, "cached_input_tokens": 0, "output_tokens": 0, "reasoning_tokens": 0,
           "cost_usd_this_run": 0.0, "cost_usd_if_uncached": 0.0}
    for st in stats.values():
        tot["model_calls"] += st["model_calls"]
        tot["cache_hits"] += int(st["cached"])
        tot["fallbacks"] += int(bool(st["fallback"]))
        if st["usage"]:
            for k in ("input_tokens", "cached_input_tokens", "output_tokens", "reasoning_tokens"):
                tot[k] += st["usage"][k]
            from .llm import cost_usd
            tot["cost_usd_if_uncached"] += cost_usd(llm.model, st["usage"]) or 0.0
        tot["cost_usd_this_run"] += st["cost_usd"] or 0.0
    n = max(1, sum(1 for st in stats.values() if st["usage"]))
    tot["avg_cost_usd_per_email"] = round(tot["cost_usd_if_uncached"] / n, 5)
    tot["avg_tokens_per_email"] = round((tot["input_tokens"] + tot["output_tokens"]) / n)
    tot["cost_usd_this_run"] = round(tot["cost_usd_this_run"], 5)
    tot["cost_usd_if_uncached"] = round(tot["cost_usd_if_uncached"], 5)
    tot["wall_seconds"] = round(secs, 1)
    return {"model": llm.model, "effort": llm.effort, "prompt_version": PROMPT_VERSION, "totals": tot, "emails": stats}

                _account(stats, res2)
                record2, warns2 = finalize(em, res2.data, truncated)
                left = missing_rows(em, record2["line_items"])
                if record2["classification"] == record["classification"] and sum(map(len, left.values())) < sum(map(len, missed.values())):
                    record, warns, missed = record2, warns2, left
            except ModelUnavailable as e:
                warns.append(f"coverage retry failed: {e}")
            if missed:
                warns.append(f"model left out numbered rows after a second look (judged not requested): {missed}")
        if record["classification"] in REQUEST_CLASSES:
            _read_windows(em, record, llm, stats, warns, truncated)
            _second_read(em, record, llm, stats, warns)
        stats["warnings"] += warns
    except ModelUnavailable as e:
        stats["fallback"] = str(e)
        record = fallback(em, str(e))
    except Exception as e:  # a bug of ours must not cost the customer their answer
        stats["fallback"] = f"internal error: {type(e).__name__}: {e}"
        stats["traceback"] = traceback.format_exc(limit=5)
        record = fallback(em, f"internal error: {type(e).__name__}")
    return em, record, stats


def _read_windows(em: Email, record: dict, llm: LLM, stats: dict, warns: list[str], truncated: list[str]) -> None:
    """Long PDFs: one more cached call per window of pages; their lines are added to the record.
    A window that can't be read makes the email need review: lines would be missing."""
    seen = {(ln["source"], ln["raw"]) for ln in record["line_items"]}
    failed = []
    for part in em.parts:
        for k, w in enumerate(part.windows):
            content = build_window_input(em, part, k, record["classification"])
            req = llm.request(INSTRUCTIONS, content, schema(["body"] + [p.filename for p in em.parts]))
            try:
                res = llm.call(req, label=f"{PROMPT_VERSION}:{em.id}:{part.filename}:p{w['pages']}")
            except ModelUnavailable as e:
                failed.append(f"{part.filename} pages {w['pages']} could not be read ({e})")
                continue
            _account(stats, res)
            data = dict(res.data, classification=record["classification"])
            got, w_warns = finalize(em, data, truncated)
            warns += [f"{part.filename} p{w['pages']}: {x}" for x in w_warns]
            for ln in got["line_items"]:
                if ln["source"] != part.filename:
                    warns.append(f"{part.filename} p{w['pages']}: dropped a line credited to {ln['source']} "
                                 f"(a window may only add lines from its own pages): {ln['raw']!r}")
                elif (ln["source"], ln["raw"]) in seen:
                    warns.append(f"{part.filename} p{w['pages']}: dropped a repeat of an earlier line: {ln['raw']!r}")
                else:
                    seen.add((ln["source"], ln["raw"]))
                    record["line_items"].append(ln)
            stats.setdefault("windows", []).append(f"{part.filename} pages {w['pages']}: {len(got['line_items'])} line(s)")
    if failed:
        record["needs_review"] = True
        reasons = [r for r in (record.get("review_reason") or "").split("; ") if r]
        record["review_reason"] = "; ".join(dict.fromkeys(reasons + failed))


def _account(stats: dict, res) -> None:
    """Add one call's tokens and cost to the email's stats (a cache hit adds tokens, not cost)."""
    keys = stats.setdefault("cache_keys", [])
    keys.append(res.key)
    stats["cache_key"] = keys[0]
    stats["cached"] = res.cached if len(keys) == 1 else stats["cached"] and res.cached
    if stats["usage"] is None:
        stats["usage"] = dict(res.usage)
    else:
        for k, v in res.usage.items():
            stats["usage"][k] = stats["usage"].get(k, 0) + v
    stats["seconds"] = round(stats["seconds"] + res.seconds, 2)
    if not res.cached:
        stats["model_calls"] += 1
        stats["cost_usd"] = (stats["cost_usd"] or 0) + (res.cost_usd or 0)


def run(email_dir: Path, out_path: Path, llm: LLM, workers: int = 4, catalog: Path | None = None) -> dict:
    paths = sorted(email_dir.glob("*.eml"))
    t0 = time.monotonic()
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=max(1, workers)) as ex:
        results = list(ex.map(lambda p: process_one(p, llm), paths))

    emails = {em.id: em for em, _, _ in results}
    out = {em.id: rec for em, rec, _ in results}
    stats = {em.id: st for em, _, st in results}
    try:
        link(emails, out)
    except Exception as e:  # links are a nice-to-have; never lose the per-email answers over them
        for st in stats.values():
            st["warnings"].append(f"thread linking failed: {e}")

    # attention: non-requests that still need a person (code only; needs_review stays per README)
    add_attention(emails, out, stats)

    # catalog matching is code only (no model calls), so it runs on every replay as well
    matching = None
    if catalog is not None and catalog.is_file():
        try:
            match_all(out, load_catalog(catalog))
            matching = dict(Counter(ln["match"] for rec in out.values() for ln in rec["line_items"]))
        except Exception as e:  # optional; never lose the parse over it
            matching = {"error": f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"}

    out_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    # "\n" on every OS: the same inbox gives the same bytes on Windows, Linux, WSL and Docker
    out_path.write_text(json.dumps(out, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
    report = _report(stats, llm, time.monotonic() - t0)
    report["totals"]["catalog_matching"] = matching
    report["totals"]["attention"] = sum(1 for rec in out.values() if rec.get("attention"))
    out_path.with_name(out_path.stem + ".report.json").write_text(
        json.dumps(report, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n"
    )
    return report


def _report(stats: dict, llm: LLM, secs: float) -> dict:
    tot = {"emails": len(stats), "model_calls": 0, "cache_hits": 0, "fallbacks": 0,
           "input_tokens": 0, "cached_input_tokens": 0, "output_tokens": 0, "reasoning_tokens": 0,
           "cost_usd_this_run": 0.0, "cost_usd_if_uncached": 0.0}
    for st in stats.values():
        tot["model_calls"] += st["model_calls"]
        tot["cache_hits"] += int(st["cached"])
        tot["fallbacks"] += int(bool(st["fallback"]))
        if st["usage"]:
            for k in ("input_tokens", "cached_input_tokens", "output_tokens", "reasoning_tokens"):
                tot[k] += st["usage"][k]
            from .llm import cost_usd
            tot["cost_usd_if_uncached"] += cost_usd(llm.model, st["usage"]) or 0.0
        tot["cost_usd_this_run"] += st["cost_usd"] or 0.0
    n = max(1, sum(1 for st in stats.values() if st["usage"]))
    tot["avg_cost_usd_per_email"] = round(tot["cost_usd_if_uncached"] / n, 5)
    tot["avg_tokens_per_email"] = round((tot["input_tokens"] + tot["output_tokens"]) / n)
    tot["cost_usd_this_run"] = round(tot["cost_usd_this_run"], 5)
    tot["cost_usd_if_uncached"] = round(tot["cost_usd_if_uncached"], 5)
    tot["wall_seconds"] = round(secs, 1)
    return {"model": llm.model, "effort": llm.effort, "prompt_version": PROMPT_VERSION, "totals": tot, "emails": stats}

You are double-checking how pictures in a customer email were read. Pictures are photos, \
scans and screenshots: handwritten lists, phone photos of printed lists, scanned forms, \
nameplates. Read ONLY the pictures; the email text is there for context.

For every item the customer is asking for that appears in a picture, return:
- source: the picture's attachment filename
- raw: the line as written in the picture (a table row's cells on one line), unchanged
- qty: the quantity written in the picture for that item, as a number; null if the picture \
shows no quantity for it (for example a nameplate, where the quantity is in the email text)

Leave out headings, column headers, totals, prices, signatures and crossed-out lines. If a \
character is hard to read, give your best reading; do not guess items that are not there.
"""


def build_reread(em: Email) -> tuple[list[dict], dict] | None:
    """The email's text and only its pictures, for an independent second reading."""
    pics = [p for p in em.parts if p.images]
    if not pics:
        return None
    content: list[dict] = [{"type": "input_text", "text": f"Subject: {em.subject}\n\n=== EMAIL TEXT ===\n"
                                                          f"{(em.body or '')[:20000]}"}]
    n = 0
    for p in pics:
        for im in p.images:
            if n >= MAX_IMAGES:
                break
            n += 1
            content.append({"type": "input_text", "text": f"[picture from attachment {p.filename!r}: {im.label}]"})
            content.append({"type": "input_image", "image_url": _data_url(im.mime, im.data), "detail": "high"})
    schema = {
        "type": "object", "additionalProperties": False, "required": ["lines"],
        "properties": {"lines": {"type": "array", "items": {
            "type": "object", "additionalProperties": False, "required": ["source", "raw", "qty"],
            "properties": {"source": {"type": "string", "enum": [p.filename for p in pics]},
                           "raw": {"type": "string"},

"""Legacy Microsoft formats inside an OLE compound file: Outlook .msg and Word 97-2003 .doc.

Both readers were checked against independent tools (extract-msg, antiword) on real files from
Apache POI's test data (tests/fixtures/legacy/, see NOTICE there).

.msg  The message's own text (subject, from, to, date, body) becomes the Part's text; each
      attachment becomes its own Part, read by the normal readers. An Outlook message attached
      inside the message is unpacked the same way, recursively.
.doc  The text is rebuilt from the document's piece table (the order Word stores text in), with
      table rows as "a | b | c". Character formatting is NOT read, so a struck-through line or an
      unaccepted tracked deletion looks like ordinary text: the Part says so, and the email is
      flagged for review (lines are still extracted).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import io
import re
import struct
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone

DOC_NO_FORMATTING = "legacy .doc read as plain text: strikethrough and tracked deletions are not visible"


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- Outlook .msg


def is_msg(data: bytes) -> bool:
    try:
        import olefile

        ole = olefile.OleFileIO(io.BytesIO(data))
        return ole.exists("__properties_version1.0") and (ole.exists("__substg1.0_0037001F") or ole.exists("__substg1.0_0037001E")
                                                          or ole.exists("__substg1.0_1000001F") or ole.exists("__substg1.0_1000001E")
                                                          or any(e[0].startswith("__attach_version1.0_") for e in ole.listdir()))
    except Exception:
        return False


def _str(ole, prefix: list[str], tag: str) -> str:
    for kind, enc in (("001F", "utf-16-le"), ("001E", "cp1252")):
        path = prefix + [f"__substg1.0_{tag}{kind}"]
        if ole.exists(path):
            return ole.openstream(path).read().decode(enc, "replace").rstrip("\x00").strip()
    return ""


def _bin(ole, prefix: list[str], tag: str) -> bytes | None:
    path = prefix + [f"__substg1.0_{tag}0102"]
    return ole.openstream(path).read() if ole.exists(path) else None


def _time(ole, prefix: list[str], header: int) -> str:
    """PR_CLIENT_SUBMIT_TIME (0x0039) or PR_MESSAGE_DELIVERY_TIME (0x0E06) from the property stream."""
    path = prefix + ["__properties_version1.0"]
    if not ole.exists(path):
        return ""
    raw = ole.openstream(path).read()
    found = {}
    for off in range(header, len(raw) - 15, 16):
        tag, _flags, value = struct.unpack_from("<IIQ", raw, off)
        if tag in (0x00390040, 0x0E060040) and value:
            found[tag] = datetime(1601, 1, 1, tzinfo=timezone.utc) + timedelta(microseconds=value // 10)
    t = found.get(0x00390040) or found.get(0x0E060040)
    return t.strftime("%a, %d %b %Y %H:%M:%S +0000") if t else ""


def read_msg(data: bytes, html_to_text) -> tuple[str, list[tuple[str, str, bytes | None, str | None]]]:
    """-> (the message as text, [(attachment name, mime, bytes, or None + text of an embedded message)])."""
    import olefile

    ole = olefile.OleFileIO(io.BytesIO(data))
    return _msg_storage(ole, [], 32, html_to_text)


def _msg_storage(ole, prefix: list[str], header: int, html_to_text):
    sender = _str(ole, prefix, "0C1A")
    addr = _str(ole, prefix, "5D01") or _str(ole, prefix, "0C1F")
    head = [
        ("From", f"{sender} <{addr}>" if sender and addr and "@" in addr else sender or addr),
        ("To", _str(ole, prefix, "0E04")),
        ("Cc", _str(ole, prefix, "0E03")),
        ("Date", _time(ole, prefix, header)),
        ("Subject", _str(ole, prefix, "0037")),
    ]
    body = _str(ole, prefix, "1000")
    html = _bin(ole, prefix, "1013")
    if html and (not body or re.search(rb"<(s|strike|del)\b|line-through", html, re.I)):
        body = html_to_text(html.decode("utf-8", "replace") if html[:3] == b"\xef\xbb\xbf" or b"charset=utf-8" in html[:2000].lower()
                            else html.decode("cp1252", "replace"))
    text = "\n".join(f"{k}: {v}" for k, v in head if v) + "\n\n" + body.strip()

    atts = []
    stems = sorted({e[len(prefix)] for e in ole.listdir() if len(e) > len(prefix) and e[:len(prefix)] == prefix
                    and e[len(prefix)].startswith("__attach_version1.0_")})
    for stem in stems:
        ap = prefix + [stem]
        name = _str(ole, ap, "3707") or _str(ole, ap, "3704") or _str(ole, ap, "3001") or f"{stem[-8:]}.bin"
        mime = _str(ole, ap, "370E") or "application/octet-stream"
        if ole.exists(ap + ["__substg1.0_3701000D"]):  # an Outlook message attached inside this one
            inner_text, inner_atts = _msg_storage(ole, ap + ["__substg1.0_3701000D"], 24, html_to_text)
            subj = re.search(r"^Subject: (.+)$", inner_text, re.M)
            atts.append(((name if name.lower().endswith(".msg") else f"{subj[1] if subj else name}.msg"),
                         "application/vnd.ms-outlook", None, inner_text))
            atts.extend(inner_atts)
            continue
        blob = _bin(ole, ap, "3701")
        if blob is not None:
            atts.append((name, mime, blob, None))
    return text, atts


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- Word 97-2003 .doc


def is_doc(data: bytes) -> bool:
    try:
        import olefile

        return olefile.OleFileIO(io.BytesIO(data)).exists("WordDocument")
    except Exception:
        return False

    import olefile

    ole = olefile.OleFileIO(io.BytesIO(data))
    wd = ole.openstream("WordDocument").read()
    if struct.unpack_from("<H", wd, 0)[0] != 0xA5EC:
        raise ValueError("not a Word 97-2003 document")
    flags = struct.unpack_from("<H", wd, 0x0A)[0]
    if flags & 0x0100:
        raise ValueError("the .doc is password-protected (encrypted)")
    table = ole.openstream("1Table" if flags & 0x0200 else "0Table").read()

    # FIB: FibBase (32 bytes), then the variable-length fibRgW, fibRgLw and fibRgFcLcb arrays
    pos = 32
    csw = struct.unpack_from("<H", wd, pos)[0]
    pos += 2 + csw * 2
    cslw = struct.unpack_from("<H", wd, pos)[0]
    ccp_text = struct.unpack_from("<i", wd, pos + 2 + 3 * 4)[0]  # FibRgLw97.ccpText: main-document length
    pos += 2 + cslw * 4
    pos += 2  # cbRgFcLcb
    fc_clx, lcb_clx = struct.unpack_from("<II", wd, pos + 33 * 8)  # FibRgFcLcb97.fcClx / lcbClx

    # Clx: skip Prc (0x01) records, then the Pcdt (0x02) holding the piece table
    clx = table[fc_clx:fc_clx + lcb_clx]
    i = 0
    while i < len(clx) and clx[i] == 0x01:
        i += 3 + struct.unpack_from("<h", clx, i + 1)[0]
    if i >= len(clx) or clx[i] != 0x02:
        raise ValueError("no piece table in this .doc")
    lcb = struct.unpack_from("<I", clx, i + 1)[0]
    plc = clx[i + 5:i + 5 + lcb]
    n = (lcb - 4) // 12
    cps = struct.unpack_from(f"<{n + 1}i", plc, 0)
    out = []
    for k in range(n):
        fc = struct.unpack_from("<I", plc, 4 * (n + 1) + 8 * k + 2)[0]
        length = cps[k + 1] - cps[k]
        if fc & 0x40000000:  # compressed: one byte per character, cp1252
            off = (fc & 0x3FFFFFFF) // 2
            out.append(wd[off:off + length].decode("cp1252", "replace"))
        else:
            off = fc & 0x3FFFFFFF
            out.append(wd[off:off + 2 * length].decode("utf-16-le", "replace"))
    return _clean_doc_text("".join(out)[:max(ccp_text, 0)])


def _clean_doc_text(t: str) -> str:
    t = re.sub(r"\x13[^\x13\x14\x15]*\x14", "", t)  # field code -> keep the field's shown result
    t = re.sub(r"\x13[^\x13\x14\x15]*\x15", "", t)  # field with no result
    t = t.replace("\x15", "")
    t = t.replace("\x07\x07", "\x07\n")  # end of a table row
    t = t.replace("\r", "\n").replace("\x0b", "\n").replace("\x0c", "\n")
    t = t.replace("\x1e", "-").replace("\x1f", "").replace("\xa0", " ")
    t = re.sub(r"[\x00-\x06\x08\x0e-\x12\x16-\x1d]", "", t)
    lines = []
    for line in t.split("\n"):
        if "\x07" in line:  # table cells
            cells = [c.strip() for c in line.split("\x07")]
            while cells and not cells[-1]:
                cells.pop()
            line = " | ".join(cells)
        lines.append(line.rstrip())
    return re.sub(r"\n{3,}", "\n\n", "\n".join(lines)).strip()

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- Word 97-2003 .doc


def is_doc(data: bytes) -> bool:
    try:
        import olefile

        return olefile.OleFileIO(io.BytesIO(data)).exists("WordDocument")
    except Exception:
        return False


def read_doc(data: bytes) -> str:
    import olefile

    ole = olefile.OleFileIO(io.BytesIO(data))
    wd = ole.openstream("WordDocument").read()
    if struct.unpack_from("<H", wd, 0)[0] != 0xA5EC:
        raise ValueError("not a Word 97-2003 document")
    flags = struct.unpack_from("<H", wd, 0x0A)[0]
    if flags & 0x0100:
        raise ValueError("the .doc is password-protected (encrypted)")
    table = ole.openstream("1Table" if flags & 0x0200 else "0Table").read()

    # FIB: FibBase (32 bytes), then the variable-length fibRgW, fibRgLw and fibRgFcLcb arrays
    pos = 32
    csw = struct.unpack_from("<H", wd, pos)[0]
    pos += 2 + csw * 2
    cslw = struct.unpack_from("<H", wd, pos)[0]
    ccp_text = struct.unpack_from("<i", wd, pos + 2 + 3 * 4)[0]  # FibRgLw97.ccpText: main-document length
    pos += 2 + cslw * 4
    pos += 2  # cbRgFcLcb
    fc_clx, lcb_clx = struct.unpack_from("<II", wd, pos + 33 * 8)  # FibRgFcLcb97.fcClx / lcbClx

    # Clx: skip Prc (0x01) records, then the Pcdt (0x02) holding the piece table
    clx = table[fc_clx:fc_clx + lcb_clx]
    i = 0
    while i < len(clx) and clx[i] == 0x01:
        i += 3 + struct.unpack_from("<h", clx, i + 1)[0]
    if i >= len(clx) or clx[i] != 0x02:
        raise ValueError("no piece table in this .doc")
    lcb = struct.unpack_from("<I", clx, i + 1)[0]
    plc = clx[i + 5:i + 5 + lcb]
    n = (lcb - 4) // 12
    cps = struct.unpack_from(f"<{n + 1}i", plc, 0)
    out = []
    for k in range(n):
        fc = struct.unpack_from("<I", plc, 4 * (n + 1) + 8 * k + 2)[0]
        length = cps[k + 1] - cps[k]
        if fc & 0x40000000:  # compressed: one byte per character, cp1252
            off = (fc & 0x3FFFFFFF) // 2
            out.append(wd[off:off + length].decode("cp1252", "replace"))
        else:
            off = fc & 0x3FFFFFFF
            out.append(wd[off:off + 2 * length].decode("utf-16-le", "replace"))
    return _clean_doc_text("".join(out)[:max(ccp_text, 0)])


def _clean_doc_text(t: str) -> str:
    t = re.sub(r"\x13[^\x13\x14\x15]*\x14", "", t)  # field code -> keep the field's shown result
    t = re.sub(r"\x13[^\x13\x14\x15]*\x15", "", t)  # field with no result
    t = t.replace("\x15", "")
    t = t.replace("\x07\x07", "\x07\n")  # end of a table row
    t = t.replace("\r", "\n").replace("\x0b", "\n").replace("\x0c", "\n")
    t = t.replace("\x1e", "-").replace("\x1f", "").replace("\xa0", " ")
    t = re.sub(r"[\x00-\x06\x08\x0e-\x12\x16-\x1d]", "", t)
    lines = []
    for line in t.split("\n"):
        if "\x07" in line:  # table cells
            cells = [c.strip() for c in line.split("\x07")]
            while cells and not cells[-1]:
                cells.pop()
            line = " | ".join(cells)
        lines.append(line.rstrip())
    return re.sub(r"\n{3,}", "\n\n", "\n".join(lines)).strip()

"""Legacy Microsoft formats inside an OLE compound file: Outlook .msg and Word 97-2003 .doc.

Both readers were checked against independent tools (extract-msg, antiword) on real files from
Apache POI's test data (tests/fixtures/legacy/, see NOTICE there).

.msg  The message's own text (subject, from, to, date, body) becomes the Part's text; each
      attachment becomes its own Part, read by the normal readers. An Outlook message attached
      inside the message is unpacked the same way, recursively.
.doc  The text is rebuilt from the document's piece table (the order Word stores text in), with
      table rows as "a | b | c". Character formatting is NOT read, so a struck-through line or an
      unaccepted tracked deletion looks like ordinary text: the Part says so, and the email is
      flagged for review (lines are still extracted).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import io
import re
import struct
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone

DOC_NO_FORMATTING = "legacy .doc read as plain text: strikethrough and tracked deletions are not visible"


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- Outlook .msg


def is_msg(data: bytes) -> bool:
    try:
        import olefile

        ole = olefile.OleFileIO(io.BytesIO(data))
        return ole.exists("__properties_version1.0") and (ole.exists("__substg1.0_0037001F") or ole.exists("__substg1.0_0037001E")
                                                          or ole.exists("__substg1.0_1000001F") or ole.exists("__substg1.0_1000001E")
                                                          or any(e[0].startswith("__attach_version1.0_") for e in ole.listdir()))
    except Exception:
        return False


def _str(ole, prefix: list[str], tag: str) -> str:
    for kind, enc in (("001F", "utf-16-le"), ("001E", "cp1252")):
        path = prefix + [f"__substg1.0_{tag}{kind}"]
        if ole.exists(path):
            return ole.openstream(path).read().decode(enc, "replace").rstrip("\x00").strip()
    return ""


def _bin(ole, prefix: list[str], tag: str) -> bytes | None:
    path = prefix + [f"__substg1.0_{tag}0102"]
    return ole.openstream(path).read() if ole.exists(path) else None


def _time(ole, prefix: list[str], header: int) -> str:
    """PR_CLIENT_SUBMIT_TIME (0x0039) or PR_MESSAGE_DELIVERY_TIME (0x0E06) from the property stream."""
    path = prefix + ["__properties_version1.0"]
    if not ole.exists(path):
        return ""
    raw = ole.openstream(path).read()
    found = {}
    for off in range(header, len(raw) - 15, 16):
        tag, _flags, value = struct.unpack_from("<IIQ", raw, off)
        if tag in (0x00390040, 0x0E060040) and value:
            found[tag] = datetime(1601, 1, 1, tzinfo=timezone.utc) + timedelta(microseconds=value // 10)
    t = found.get(0x00390040) or found.get(0x0E060040)
    return t.strftime("%a, %d %b %Y %H:%M:%S +0000") if t else ""


def read_msg(data: bytes, html_to_text) -> tuple[str, list[tuple[str, str, bytes | None, str | None]]]:
    """-> (the message as text, [(attachment name, mime, bytes, or None + text of an embedded message)])."""
    import olefile

    ole = olefile.OleFileIO(io.BytesIO(data))
    return _msg_storage(ole, [], 32, html_to_text)


def _msg_storage(ole, prefix: list[str], header: int, html_to_text):
    sender = _str(ole, prefix, "0C1A")
    addr = _str(ole, prefix, "5D01") or _str(ole, prefix, "0C1F")
    head = [
        ("From", f"{sender} <{addr}>" if sender and addr and "@" in addr else sender or addr),
        ("To", _str(ole, prefix, "0E04")),
        ("Cc", _str(ole, prefix, "0E03")),
        ("Date", _time(ole, prefix, header)),
        ("Subject", _str(ole, prefix, "0037")),
    ]
    body = _str(ole, prefix, "1000")
    html = _bin(ole, prefix, "1013")
    if html and (not body or re.search(rb"<(s|strike|del)\b|line-through", html, re.I)):
        body = html_to_text(html.decode("utf-8", "replace") if html[:3] == b"\xef\xbb\xbf" or b"charset=utf-8" in html[:2000].lower()
                            else html.decode("cp1252", "replace"))
    text = "\n".join(f"{k}: {v}" for k, v in head if v) + "\n\n" + body.strip()

    atts = []
    stems = sorted({e[len(prefix)] for e in ole.listdir() if len(e) > len(prefix) and e[:len(prefix)] == prefix
                    and e[len(prefix)].startswith("__attach_version1.0_")})
    for stem in stems:
        ap = prefix + [stem]
        name = _str(ole, ap, "3707") or _str(ole, ap, "3704") or _str(ole, ap, "3001") or f"{stem[-8:]}.bin"
        mime = _str(ole, ap, "370E") or "application/octet-stream"
        if ole.exists(ap + ["__substg1.0_3701000D"]):  # an Outlook message attached inside this one
            inner_text, inner_atts = _msg_storage(ole, ap + ["__substg1.0_3701000D"], 24, html_to_text)
            subj = re.search(r"^Subject: (.+)$", inner_text, re.M)
            atts.append(((name if name.lower().endswith(".msg") else f"{subj[1] if subj else name}.msg"),
                         "application/vnd.ms-outlook", None, inner_text))
            atts.extend(inner_atts)
            continue
        blob = _bin(ole, ap, "3701")
        if blob is not None:
            atts.append((name, mime, blob, None))
    return text, atts


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- Word 97-2003 .doc


def is_doc(data: bytes) -> bool:
    try:
        import olefile

        return olefile.OleFileIO(io.BytesIO(data)).exists("WordDocument")
    except Exception:
        return False


def read_doc(data: bytes) -> str:
    import olefile

    ole = olefile.OleFileIO(io.BytesIO(data))
    wd = ole.openstream("WordDocument").read()
    if struct.unpack_from("<H", wd, 0)[0] != 0xA5EC:
        raise ValueError("not a Word 97-2003 document")
    flags = struct.unpack_from("<H", wd, 0x0A)[0]
    if flags & 0x0100:
        raise ValueError("the .doc is password-protected (encrypted)")
    table = ole.openstream("1Table" if flags & 0x0200 else "0Table").read()

    # FIB: FibBase (32 bytes), then the variable-length fibRgW, fibRgLw and fibRgFcLcb arrays
    pos = 32
    csw = struct.unpack_from("<H", wd, pos)[0]
    pos += 2 + csw * 2
    cslw = struct.unpack_from("<H", wd, pos)[0]
    ccp_text = struct.unpack_from("<i", wd, pos + 2 + 3 * 4)[0]  # FibRgLw97.ccpText: main-document length
    pos += 2 + cslw * 4
    pos += 2  # cbRgFcLcb
    fc_clx, lcb_clx = struct.unpack_from("<II", wd, pos + 33 * 8)  # FibRgFcLcb97.fcClx / lcbClx

    # Clx: skip Prc (0x01) records, then the Pcdt (0x02) holding the piece table
    clx = table[fc_clx:fc_clx + lcb_clx]
    i = 0
    while i < len(clx) and clx[i] == 0x01:
        i += 3 + struct.unpack_from("<h", clx, i + 1)[0]
    if i >= len(clx) or clx[i] != 0x02:
        raise ValueError("no piece table in this .doc")
    lcb = struct.unpack_from("<I", clx, i + 1)[0]
    plc = clx[i + 5:i + 5 + lcb]
    n = (lcb - 4) // 12
    cps = struct.unpack_from(f"<{n + 1}i", plc, 0)
    out = []
    for k in range(n):
        fc = struct.unpack_from("<I", plc, 4 * (n + 1) + 8 * k + 2)[0]
        length = cps[k + 1] - cps[k]
        if fc & 0x40000000:  # compressed: one byte per character, cp1252
            off = (fc & 0x3FFFFFFF) // 2
            out.append(wd[off:off + length].decode("cp1252", "replace"))
        else:
            off = fc & 0x3FFFFFFF
            out.append(wd[off:off + 2 * length].decode("utf-16-le", "replace"))
    return _clean_doc_text("".join(out)[:max(ccp_text, 0)])


def _clean_doc_text(t: str) -> str:
    t = re.sub(r"\x13[^\x13\x14\x15]*\x14", "", t)  # field code -> keep the field's shown result
    t = re.sub(r"\x13[^\x13\x14\x15]*\x15", "", t)  # field with no result
    t = t.replace("\x15", "")
    t = t.replace("\x07\x07", "\x07\n")  # end of a table row
    t = t.replace("\r", "\n").replace("\x0b", "\n").replace("\x0c", "\n")
    t = t.replace("\x1e", "-").replace("\x1f", "").replace("\xa0", " ")
    t = re.sub(r"[\x00-\x06\x08\x0e-\x12\x16-\x1d]", "", t)
    lines = []
    for line in t.split("\n"):
        if "\x07" in line:  # table cells
            cells = [c.strip() for c in line.split("\x07")]
            while cells and not cells[-1]:
                cells.pop()
            line = " | ".join(cells)
        lines.append(line.rstrip())
    return re.sub(r"\n{3,}", "\n\n", "\n".join(lines)).strip()

"""Outlook .msg and Word 97-2003 .doc, on real files from Apache POI's test data.

Expected values come from independent tools run on the same files (antiword for .doc,
extract-msg for .msg), not from our own reader. See tests/fixtures/legacy/NOTICE.md.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

from rfq.guards import finalize
from rfq.ingest import load_email
from rfq.legacy import DOC_NO_FORMATTING
from tests.test_ingest import _eml

FIX = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "fixtures" / "legacy"


def parts(tmp_path, name, mime="application/octet-stream", as_name=None):
    em = load_email(_eml(tmp_path, [(as_name or name, mime, (FIX / name).read_bytes())]))
    return em, {p.filename: p for p in em.parts}


# ---- .doc (antiword's output)


def test_doc_text_matches_antiword(tmp_path):
    _, ps = parts(tmp_path, "SampleDoc.doc", "application/msword")
    t = ps["SampleDoc.doc"].text
    for line in ("I am a test document", "This is page two", "It’s Arial Black in 16 point", "It’s also in blue"):
        assert line in t


def test_doc_table_rows_match_antiword(tmp_path):
    _, ps = parts(tmp_path, "simple-table.doc", "application/msword")
    t = ps["simple-table.doc"].text
    assert "Cell 1,1 | Cell 1,2 | Cell 1,3" in t and "Cell 2,1 | Cell 2,2 | Cell 2,3" in t
    assert "This text is below the table." in t


def test_doc_says_formatting_is_not_visible_and_the_request_is_flagged(tmp_path):
    em, ps = parts(tmp_path, "simple-table.doc", "application/msword")
    assert DOC_NO_FORMATTING in ps["simple-table.doc"].notes
    data = {"classification": "rfq", "needs_review": False, "review_reason": None,
            "line_items": [{"raw": "Cell 1,1 | Cell 1,2 | Cell 1,3", "description": "x", "qty": 1, "uom": None,
                            "source": "simple-table.doc"}]}
    rec, _ = finalize(em, data, [])
    assert rec["needs_review"] and "strikethrough" in rec["review_reason"] and rec["line_items"], \
        "lines are read, and a person checks for crossed-out ones"


def test_doc_with_a_wrong_name_is_read_by_content(tmp_path):
    _, ps = parts(tmp_path, "SampleDoc.doc", as_name="scan0001.bin")
    assert "This is page two" in ps["scan0001.bin"].text


# ---- .msg (extract-msg's output)


def test_msg_headers_body_and_attachments_match_extract_msg(tmp_path):
    _, ps = parts(tmp_path, "attachment_test_msg.msg", "application/vnd.ms-outlook")
    t = ps["attachment_test_msg.msg"].text
    assert "Subject: test pièce jointe 1" in t and "Wed, 22 Apr 2009 14:36:33" in t and "contenu" in t
    assert "nicolas1.23456@free.fr" in t
    assert {"test-unicode.doc", "pj1.txt"} <= set(ps)
    doc = ps["test-unicode.doc"]
    assert "found inside attachment_test_msg.msg" in doc.notes
    assert "€ (20AC)" in doc.text and "école (00E9)" in doc.text  # the file names its own code points


def test_msg_inside_msg_and_its_pdf(tmp_path):
    _, ps = parts(tmp_path, "attachment_msg_pdf.msg", "application/vnd.ms-outlook")
    outer = ps["attachment_msg_pdf.msg"].text
    assert "nick.booth@pof.com.au" in outer, "address found in the transport headers"
    assert "Thu, 17 Jun 2010 23:54:19" in outer and "Test email with 1 msg attachment, 1 pdf" in outer
    inner = ps["Test Attachment.msg"]
    assert "Blah blah blah" in inner.text and "Thu, 17 Jun 2010 23:52:19" in inner.text
    assert "smbprn.00009008.KdcPjl.pdf" in ps and ps["smbprn.00009008.KdcPjl.pdf"].kind == "text"


def test_msg_ansi_strings_and_exchange_names(tmp_path):
    _, ps = parts(tmp_path, "quick.msg")  # no .msg type given: recognised by content
    t = ps["quick.msg"].text
    assert "Subject: Test the content transformer" in t and "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog" in t
    assert "/O=" not in t, "an Exchange X.500 name is not an email address"

"""Attachment types the dev inbox doesn't show, generated here: zip archives (nested, bombs,
passwords), Office files with a wrong or missing extension, legacy .xls, iPhone HEIC photos,
sideways phone photos, oversized photos, and the legacy types we deliberately don't read.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import io
import zipfile
from pathlib import Path

import pytest
from PIL import Image as PILImage

from rfq.ingest import MAX_ARCHIVE_FILES, MAX_IMAGE_SIDE, STRIKE_L, load_email
from tests.test_ingest import _eml

XLSX = "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet"


def _xlsx_bytes() -> bytes:
    import openpyxl

    wb = openpyxl.Workbook()
    ws = wb.active
    ws.title = "BOM"
    ws.append(["Item", "Qty", "Description"])
    ws.append([1, 12, '2" 90 elbow SCH 40 BW'])
    buf = io.BytesIO()
    wb.save(buf)
    return buf.getvalue()


def _zip(files: dict[str, bytes]) -> bytes:
    buf = io.BytesIO()
    with zipfile.ZipFile(buf, "w", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as z:
        for n, d in files.items():
            z.writestr(n, d)
    return buf.getvalue()


def _jpeg(w=400, h=200, orientation=None) -> bytes:
    im = PILImage.new("RGB", (w, h), "white")
    buf = io.BytesIO()
    exif = PILImage.Exif()
    if orientation:
        exif[0x0112] = orientation
    im.save(buf, "JPEG", exif=exif.tobytes())
    return buf.getvalue()


def _parts(tmp_path, attachments):
    return {p.filename: p for p in load_email(_eml(tmp_path, attachments)).parts}


# ---- zip


def test_zip_members_become_their_own_attachments(tmp_path):
    z = _zip({"drawings/BOM.xlsx": _xlsx_bytes(), "notes.csv": b"Qty,Item\n4,2\" cap\n", "__MACOSX/._BOM.xlsx": b"junk"})
    parts = _parts(tmp_path, [("job.zip", "application/zip", z)])
    assert set(parts) == {"job.zip", "BOM.xlsx", "notes.csv"}
    assert parts["job.zip"].kind == "skipped"
    assert '12 | 2" 90 elbow SCH 40 BW' in parts["BOM.xlsx"].text
    assert "found inside job.zip" in parts["BOM.xlsx"].notes


def test_zip_inside_zip_is_unpacked_to_a_limit(tmp_path):
    inner = _zip({"list.csv": b"Qty,Item\n1,tee\n"})
    parts = _parts(tmp_path, [("outer.zip", "application/zip", _zip({"inner.zip": inner}))])
    assert "list.csv" in parts and parts["list.csv"].kind == "text"
    deep = _zip({"a.zip": _zip({"b.zip": _zip({"c.csv": b"x,y\n1,2\n"})})})
    parts = _parts(tmp_path, [("deep.zip", "application/zip", deep)])
    assert "c.csv" not in parts and any(p.kind == "unreadable" for p in parts.values())


def test_zip_bomb_is_refused_not_unpacked(tmp_path):
    z = _zip({f"f{i}.txt": b"x" for i in range(MAX_ARCHIVE_FILES + 1)})
    parts = _parts(tmp_path, [("many.zip", "application/zip", z)])
    assert list(parts) == ["many.zip"] and parts["many.zip"].kind == "unreadable"


def test_password_protected_zip_member_is_flagged(tmp_path):
    z = bytearray(_zip({"secret.xlsx": _xlsx_bytes()}))
    # set the "encrypted" flag bit in the local and central headers (zipfile can't write encryption)
    for sig, off in ((b"PK\x03\x04", 6), (b"PK\x01\x02", 8)):
        i = z.find(sig)
        z[i + off] |= 0x01
    parts = _parts(tmp_path, [("locked.zip", "application/zip", bytes(z))])
    assert parts["secret.xlsx"].kind == "unreadable"
    assert "password" in " ".join(parts["secret.xlsx"].notes)


def test_office_file_with_wrong_or_no_extension_is_read_by_content(tmp_path):
    parts = _parts(tmp_path, [("BOM", "application/octet-stream", _xlsx_bytes()),
                              ("export.dat", "application/octet-stream", _xlsx_bytes())])
    assert all('2" 90 elbow' in p.text for p in parts.values())


# ---- legacy Excel


def test_legacy_xls_keeps_hidden_sheets_rows_and_strike(tmp_path):
    xlwt = pytest.importorskip("xlwt")
    wb = xlwt.Workbook()
    ws = wb.add_sheet("Rev C")
    struck = xlwt.easyxf("font: struck_out on")
    ws.write(0, 0, "ALL PIPE SCH 40")
    for c, v in enumerate([1, 10, '2" pipe']):
        ws.write(1, c, v)
    for c, v in enumerate([2, 4, '3" pipe']):
        ws.write(2, c, v, struck)
    for c, v in enumerate([3, 6, '4" pipe']):
        ws.write(3, c, v)
    ws.row(3).hidden = True
    old = wb.add_sheet("Rev B")
    old.write(0, 0, '6" pipe')
    old.visibility = 1
    buf = io.BytesIO()
    wb.save(buf)
    (p,) = _parts(tmp_path, [("bom.xls", "application/vnd.ms-excel", buf.getvalue())]).values()
    assert p.kind == "text"
    assert '1 | 10 | 2" pipe' in p.visible_rows
    assert f'{STRIKE_L}3" pipe' in p.text
    assert "[HIDDEN ROW]" in p.text and '3 | 6 | 4" pipe' in p.hidden_rows
    assert "[HIDDEN SHEET]" in p.text and '6" pipe' in p.hidden_rows


# ---- photos


def test_iphone_heic_photo_is_read(tmp_path):
    pillow_heif = pytest.importorskip("pillow_heif")
    pillow_heif.register_heif_opener()
    buf = io.BytesIO()
    PILImage.new("RGB", (640, 480), "white").save(buf, "HEIF")
    (p,) = _parts(tmp_path, [("IMG_1234.HEIC", "image/heic", buf.getvalue())]).values()
    assert p.kind == "image" and p.images[0].mime == "image/jpeg"


def test_sideways_phone_photo_is_turned_upright(tmp_path):
    (p,) = _parts(tmp_path, [("IMG_2.jpg", "image/jpeg", _jpeg(400, 200, orientation=6))]).values()
    im = PILImage.open(io.BytesIO(p.images[0].data))
    assert im.size == (200, 400), "orientation 6 = rotate 90: width and height swap"
    assert any("rotated upright" in n for n in p.notes)


def test_upright_small_jpeg_is_sent_byte_for_byte(tmp_path):
    data = _jpeg()
    (p,) = _parts(tmp_path, [("IMG_3.jpg", "image/jpeg", data)]).values()
    assert p.images[0].data == data  # unchanged bytes keep the replay cache valid


def test_oversized_photo_is_downscaled_and_stays_jpeg(tmp_path):
    (p,) = _parts(tmp_path, [("IMG_4.jpg", "image/jpeg", _jpeg(4032, 3024))]).values()
    im = PILImage.open(io.BytesIO(p.images[0].data))
    assert max(im.size) <= MAX_IMAGE_SIDE and p.images[0].mime == "image/jpeg"


# ---- types deliberately not read: flagged, with a reason


@pytest.mark.parametrize("name, mime", [("spec.doc", "application/msword"), ("fwd.msg", "application/vnd.ms-outlook")])
def test_legacy_word_and_outlook_files_are_flagged(tmp_path, name, mime):
    ole = b"\xd0\xcf\x11\xe0\xa1\xb1\x1a\xe1" + b"\x00" * 600
    (p,) = _parts(tmp_path, [(name, mime, ole)]).values()
    assert p.kind == "unreadable" and "not read automatically" in " ".join(p.notes)

All four weaknesses you pointed at are now addressed, tested, committed (latest `500bc34`) and verified on Windows and on Python 3.11 / Linux (15/15).

| Weakness | What we did | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **README allows review flag only on requests** | New `attention` field (code, $0): "our email to X bounced: resend", "customer waiting on Q-26-04417", "close Q-26-04512 as lost", "invoice INV-88412 → accounting". `needs_review` contract untouched. | All 10 non-requests match what I wrote down before building it; 8 tests |
| **Terse revisions, original not in the inbox** | Code flags a revision it can't rebuild (original missing, nothing quoted, changes by position); a quoted original gets rebuilt | S22 flagged, S23 rebuilt (#3→12, #4 removed); 7 tests |
| **Handwritten photos and scans** | Every picture read **twice**; code compares, and a different count or quantity flags the line ("read as 6 and as 8") | Handwritten S24 4/4; all 8 picture emails agree; 5 tests of the disagreement paths |
| **`.doc` / `.msg` not read** | Readers for both, tested on **real files from Apache POI**, with expected values from **antiword and extract-msg** | Embedded email, PDF, Unicode, tables all read; 7 tests |

**What we caught along the way:**
- **Three portability bugs**: Python-3.12-only syntax that wouldn't even start on the brief's minimum 3.11; Windows line endings; and a zip email that **missed its cache on Linux** because a file type came from the operating system. All fixed. `verify --linux` now proves the output is byte-identical on both systems.
- **Two of my own mistakes, caught by tests:** an invoice pattern that matched "**Inv**oice" itself, and a nameplate photo the second read split into 8 "items". The nameplate was fixed in the instructions, not with a code exception.
- **Two false alarms I nearly acted on:** "garbage" characters that were really the Unicode test file's deliberate characters, displayed badly by my console. I checked before "fixing" a correct reader.

**Totals now:** 100 tests. Dev 24/24 classes, 210/210 lines, review 100%/100%. Stress 25/25 emails, 148/148 lines, 0 hallucinated. Cost $0.0083 per email; total API spend is still about $2 of $20.

**Before submitting:**
1. **DECISIONS.md has grown back to about 1,440 words**, over two pages. I'll trim it in a final pass. AI_USAGE.md could also mention the portability catch.
2. **The recording.** The script I gave you still works, and you could add 20 seconds on `verify --linux` ("I tested it the way you'll run it").
3. **Final session-log export, re-run `verify`, then submit** (push to GitHub or zip with `.git`).

Shall I do the final trim of DECISIONS.md now?

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| dev | 24/24 | 210/210 · 210/210 | 0 | 0 | 172/173 | 100 / 100% |

  gave fixtures, checked against antiword and extract-msg. A `.doc`'s strikethrough isn't
  visible, so those emails are still flagged.

## Something in the data that surprised you

The most request-shaped text in the inbox is usually not a request.
- E013's bounce carries a perfect numbered list of valves: it is *our own* RFQ to a supplier.
- E011 is a supplier's price list.
- E005's `RevB` workbook hides a sheet `Rev A (old)`. Load every sheet and you quote both
  revisions; trust the filename and you call it a revision with no earlier email.

The real requests hide: in a merged cell two rows up (`ALL FITTINGS BW SCH 40 A234 WPB UNLESS
NOTED`, one row overriding to SCH 80), or on a nameplate photo. Most accuracy came from *ingest*
marking that structure, not from the prompt.

the catalog, with answers from the catalog table rather than my logic, found **113 confident wrong
matches** (grades matched too loosely, `A-105 class 150` read as class 105).

The README allows `needs_review` only on requests. But the brief's costliest failure is "a
customer who never hears back", and some non-requests need a person: our quote bouncing, a
customer asking where their quote is, a lost deal to close.

flag on doubt.

1. **Photos and scans.** Two readings are compared, and a different count or quantity flags the
   line ("read as 6 and as 8"). What remains is a misreading both readings share, and a picture
   `raw` that pairs badly with the key's own reading.
2. **The rfq/revision boundary.** A "kill #5" whose original is neither in the inbox nor quoted
   is flagged; a quoted original is rebuilt (stress S22/S23). The judgement remains: is Rev B /
   a resend / "also add" a new rfq or a revision? I chose "a revision changes an *earlier email*".

- a per-email cost report.

  `.eml` and enqueues its hash; workers run `process_one`; thread linking becomes a lookup in a
  store of past emails.
- **Provider down for two hours.** The breaker trips. Headers settle auto_reply and bulk;
  everything else becomes `rfq` + `needs_review`. Fallbacks aren't cached, so the next run re-calls
  exactly those. For real: hold them in the queue with an alert, because 250 emails on a desk is
  worse than a 2-hour delay.
- **A 300-page PDF.** Built: windows of 30 pages (16 if scanned), one cached call each, ~$0.30.
  Every window also gets page 1 and the previous window's end as context. A failed window flags
  review. Stress S18: 105/105 rows, where the old 30-page cap lost 15. Not done: skipping
  spec-book pages that hold no items.
- **The same email delivered twice.** Built. The redelivery hits the same cache key, so it's free,
  and `threads` marks it `duplicate_of` (stress S13). For real, dedupe at the webhook.

- Picture `raw` varies between runs (E023). The cache makes it stable, not right.
- Thread linking sees only the current inbox.
- The matcher reads only our `description`, so an upstream context miss becomes a match miss.
- Next: rep overturns as the matcher's live error rate; `attention` as the desk's queue.

# DECISIONS

**Time spent:** about 8 hours.

## Who decides what

`ingest` (code) → **one model call per email** (`gpt-5.4-mini-2026-03-17`, effort medium, strict
JSON schema) → `guards` (code) → `threads` (code) → `matcher` (code; see [MATCHER.md](MATCHER.md)).

- **Code reads the files**, keeping the structure that carries meaning: hidden sheets and rows,
  merged headings and struck cells (xlsx/xls); tracked deletions (docx); PDF rows rebuilt from
  word positions, scans sent as images; zips and Outlook `.msg` unpacked; legacy `.doc`/`.xls`;
photos turned upright, read twice when lines come from them. A broken part
  becomes `unreadable` with a reason. It never raises.
- **The model judges.** It decides the class, which lines are requests, and the self-contained
  description (heading scope, overrides beat defaults, quoted history is not a request). The prompt
  states principles; its one example is invented, not a dev row.
- **Code checks every fact it can.**
  - Struck and hidden-only lines are dropped, whatever the model said.
  - Non-requests carry no lines.
  - A request with no lines, or an unreadable part, is always `needs_review`.
  - `source` must be a real part.
  - `raw` is snapped to its unique source row, because the model's copy varies run to run.
  - A numbered row that no line covers gets one more call naming it. That caught a dropped PO line
    in E015 ($0.004).

**Measured, not guessed.** I wrote a scorer implementing the README's grading, and a 22-email
**stress inbox** of situations dev lacks, with answers written **before** each run: tracked
changes, Spanish, an invoice with item lines, "make #3 twelve and kill #5", a byte-identical
redelivery, a 35-page PDF, a BOM in a zip, an iPhone HEIC photo.

| | classes | lines (recall/precision) | silent | hallucinated | context |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| dev | 24/24 | 210/210 · 210/210 | 0 | 0 | 172/173 |
| stress | 22/22 | 141/141 · 141/141 | 0 | 0 | 140/141 |

`scripts/verify.py` re-checks all of this, the keyless replay and the hygiene rules from a fresh
clone in about 15 s.

**Rejected:** gpt-5.5 (4.6× the cost, *worse* context: it "corrected" `A53B` to `A53 Grade B`);
two calls per email (double cost, same reading). `.doc`/`.msg` readers were first rejected as
untestable, then built once real Apache POI test files gave fixtures; expected values come from
antiword and extract-msg. A `.doc`'s formatting isn't read, so a struck line can't be told
apart from a live one: those emails are still flagged, now with their lines.

## Something in the data that surprised you

The most request-shaped text in the inbox is usually not a request.
- E013's bounce carries a perfect numbered list of valves: it is *our own* RFQ to a supplier.
- E011 is a supplier's price list.
- E005's workbook is named `RevB` and hides a sheet `Rev A (old)`. A reader that loads every sheet
  quotes both revisions, and a model that sees the filename calls it a revision with no earlier
  email.

Meanwhile the real requests hide: in a merged cell two rows up (`ALL FITTINGS BW SCH 40 A234 WPB
UNLESS NOTED`, with one row overriding it to SCH 80), or on a photo of a nameplate. Most of the
accuracy came from *ingest* faithfully marking hidden, struck and merged structure, not from the
prompt.

A second surprise: **dev agrees with you too easily.** The matcher scored 210/210 on dev. A test
generated from the catalog, whose expected answers come from the catalog table and not from my
logic, then found **113 confident wrong matches**: grades matched too loosely, `A-105 class 150`
read as class 105.

## Something in the brief or README you disagree with

The README allows `needs_review` only on `rfq`, `rfq_revision` and `purchase_order`. But the
brief's costliest failure is "a customer who never hears back", and some non-requests need a
person: a bounce of *our quote to a customer*, a "we went with someone else" that should close a
quote, a buyer's out-of-office on a deadline job. Under the contract these come back `auto_reply`
/ `other` with nothing to act on.

**What I did:** kept the contract exactly (guards enforce it, because it is scored), and added a
separate field instead of bending it.
- `attention` is a one-line action, or null, for non-requests a person must act on. It's decided
  by code from the class plus evidence: "our email to sales@… ('Quote request…') was not
  delivered: fix the address and resend"; "customer is waiting for an answer about Q-26-04417";
  "close Q-26-04512 as lost"; "invoice INV-88412: route to accounting".
- Marketing and out-of-office get null, because an action list that cries wolf stops being read.

On dev and stress it matches what I wrote down before building it, on all 10 non-requests.
`check_format.py` accepts the extra field.

## Predicted held-out numbers, and two kinds of email I expect to get wrong

Dev is 100% partly because I looked at it; stress is the fairer guide. For ~40 held-out emails:

| silent | hallucinated | lost/phantom | classes | recall / precision | qty · uom · source | context | review P / R | matcher wrong · NIC recall |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **0** | **2–5** | **1–2** | **~90%** | **~90% / ~95%** | **~95 · 97 · 97%** | **~85%** | **~80 / 90%** | **0–2 · ~85%** |

Silent is 0 because code flags any request that comes back with no lines; review recall beats
precision because I flag on doubt.

1. **Photos and scans of handwritten lists.** Code can't check a picture, but it can check two
   readings against each other. Lines from pictures get an independent second reading, and a
   different count or quantity flags the email, naming the line ("quantity read as 6 and as 8").

   remains: a misreading both reads share, and a `raw` that pairs badly with the key's own reading.
2. **Revisions, at the rfq/revision boundary.** "Kill #5" with the original neither in the inbox

   S22/S23). What remains is the judgement: is Rev B / a resend / "also add" a new rfq or a revision?
   I chose "a revision only changes an *earlier email*"; held-out may draw it differently.

## How this runs for real

**Built:**
- a content-addressed cache (sha256 of model, effort, prompt and full content incl. image bytes;
  atomic writes);
- 3 retries with timeouts and a circuit breaker after 3 consecutive failures;
- a header-based fallback per email, and per-email isolation;
- windowed long PDFs;
- a per-email cost and token report.

**Not built:** the webhook, a queue, a database.

- **3,000 emails a day.** $0.0083 per email measured (about 4,430 tokens, incl. second readings of pictures), so about **$25/day**.
  Median latency is 4.9 s and the worst 24 s; 3,000/day is ~2 a minute, so one worker keeps up.
  Design: the webhook stores the raw `.eml` and enqueues its hash; workers run `process_one`;
  thread linking becomes a lookup in a store of past emails by Message-ID, subject and domain.
- **Provider down for two hours.** After the retries, the breaker trips and the rest get the
  fallback: auto_reply/bulk by header, everything else `rfq` + `needs_review`. Fallbacks aren't
  cached, so the next run re-calls exactly those. For real: hold them in the queue with backoff
  and an alert. 250 emails on a person's desk is worse than a 2-hour delay.
- **A 300-page PDF.** Built. It's read in windows of 30 pages (16 if scanned), one cached call
  each: ~10 calls, ~$0.30. Each window also gets page 1 and the previous window's end as
  context-only, because a heading on page 2 can govern page 40. A failed window flags review
  and keeps what was read; past 300 pages the rest is flagged. Stress S18: 105/105 rows (the
  old 30-page cap lost 15). Not done: a relevance pass to skip spec-book pages that hold no
  items.
- **The same email delivered twice.** Built two ways. The redelivery hashes to the same cache
  key, so it's free, and `threads` marks the later one `duplicate_of` (stress S13 is a byte copy).
  For real, dedupe on Message-ID plus body hash at the webhook.

## Known broken / next

- `raw` read from pictures varies between runs (E023). The cache makes it stable, not right.
- Thread linking only sees the current inbox; there's no memory of last week.
- The matcher reads only our `description`, so a context miss upstream becomes a match miss.
- Next: the viewer's rep overturns as the matcher's live error rate; `attention` as a queue for the desk.

# AI_USAGE

## Setup

- **Claude Code** in the VS Code extension, model **Claude Opus 5.5**, in one long session
  (`ai-sessions/92594963-78dc-4559-ba5d-13415136fa1e.jsonl`, continued across context
  compactions). The `subagents/` folder holds the one subagent: Claude Code's built-in
  **code-review** skill, which I ran over the helper scripts.
- **No CLAUDE.md, custom subagents or saved prompts.** The only standing instruction is Claude
  Code's auto-memory file for this project (`ai-sessions/memory/`). It records the deadline, that I
  wanted the *why* explained at each step, and that the API key must never be printed.
- **Tools:**
  - the agent's shell, file and web-search tools;
  - Docker, for a throwaway Python sandbox before Python was installed;
  - the claude.ai Artifact tool, for a hosted quote-desk page.

  No other MCP servers were used.
- **The parser's model** (OpenAI `gpt-5.4-mini`) ran on the assignment key. The agent never saw
  the key: it lives in a git-ignored `.env`.
